issues.issue_title: [Bug]: HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA fails when transfer size is > 65535 bytes
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA fails when transfer size is > 65535 bytes
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=343
Root cause: Hello @timkostka, Thank you for your report, it seems that point makes sense and will be tracked internally.
Fix: ### Bug Summary HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA fails when transfer size is > 65535 bytes ### Detailed Description With CRYP set up with word-sized transfers (CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_WORD), it should be able to process 65535 words, or up to 262140 bytes.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, DMA, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, cryp, HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA, CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_WORD, HAL_CRYP_Encrypt_DMA

Technical details:
### Bug Summary HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA fails when transfer size is > 65535 bytes ### Detailed Description With CRYP set up with word-sized transfers (CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_WORD), it should be able to process 65535 words, or up to 262140 bytes. Internal to HAL, the Size field is set to the number of bytes in the operation, not the number of words, which causes an overflow in the uint16_t value. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_cryp.c#L1587 /* Calculate Size parameter in Byte*/ if (hcryp->Init.DataWidthUnit == CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_WORD) { hcryp->Size = Size * 4U; } else { hcryp->Size = Size; } The comments say that Size is the number of bytes or the number of words, depending on DataWidthUnit. However, the code sets it to the number of bytes regardless of the DataWidthUnit setting. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/a1996eed9172b59887bafaaa0ea1816ea14d48b5/Inc/stm32h7xx_hal_cryp.h#L111 uint16_t Size; /*!< length of input data in word or in byte, according to DataWidthUnit */ It looks like many of the DMA functions are passed Size / 4. The same issue is present within HAL_CRYP_Encrypt_DMA and possibly others. Community post: https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-security/unexpected-behavior-of-the-stm32-cryp-module/m-p/891638#M9633 ### Expected Behavior HAL_CRYP_Decrypt_DMA functions correctly for operations on <= 65535 words when set to CRYP_DATAWIDTHUNIT_WORD ### Actual Behavior The transfer size is truncated due to the number of bytes being stored as a uint16_t ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Normal

Key comments:
Hello @timkostka, Thank you for your report, it seems that point makes sense and will be tracked internally. I'll keep you informed about last update and our decision about this point. BR, Mohamed Chaker. ST Internal Reference: CDM0061687

issues.issue_title: [Bug]: CubeMx allows an invalid combination of parameters for ADC with DMA
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: CubeMx allows an invalid combination of parameters for ADC with DMA
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H743VITX, component=ADC, layer=CubeMX, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=338
Root cause: Hello @giuliomoro, Thank you for your report, I think there is a small typo in your sentence > The issue is that if Conversion Data Management Mode is not set to ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_CIRCULAR or ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DR, then CubeMx will generate some unusable
Fix: ### Bug Summary CubeMx allows an invalid combination of parameters for ADC with DMA ### Detailed Description When DMA is enabled on an ADC, DMA requests will only be issued if ADC_InitTypeDef::ConversionDataManagement is set to ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_ONESHOT or ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_CIRCULAR.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H743VITX, CubeMX, ADC, bug_report, low, enhancement, internal bug tracker, cube mx, DMA, ADC_InitTypeDef, ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_ONESHOT

Technical details:
### Bug Summary CubeMx allows an invalid combination of parameters for ADC with DMA ### Detailed Description When DMA is enabled on an ADC, DMA requests will only be issued if ADC_InitTypeDef::ConversionDataManagement is set to ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_ONESHOT or ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_CIRCULAR. That is to say, ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DR and ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DFSDM are invalid when DMA is enabled. The issue is that if Conversion Data Management Mode is not set to ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_CIRCULAR or ~~ADC CONVERSIONDATA DR~~ ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_ONESHOT, then CubeMx will generate some unusable code. CubeMx could detect and flag this issue for the user. Or it could disable non-DMA values when DMA is enabled. Or it could make it more obvious to the user some other way that there is some DMA-relevant (and, indeed, crucial) setting in that otherwise irrelevant-looking "Conversion Data Management Mode". ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Actual Behavior _No response_ ### Environment CubeMx 6.16.1, STM32H743VITx, ADC1 ### Severity None

Key comments:
Hello @giuliomoro, Thank you for your report, I think there is a small typo in your sentence > The issue is that if Conversion Data Management Mode is not set to ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_CIRCULAR or ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DR, then CubeMx will generate some unusable code. You mean ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DMA_ONESHOT instead ADC_CONVERSIONDATA_DR ? BR, Mohamed Chaker. yes correct, I now amended the original post for clarity. Hello @giuliomoro, Thank you for your report, this point has been tracked internally. I'll keep you informed. BR, Mohamed Chaker. ST Internal Reference: CDM0060711

Root cause: Hello @rxa1031, Thank you for your report.

Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H753ZI, Middleware, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, mw, lwip, ZIP, IOC, lwIP_Ethernet_WORKS_03

Technical details:
Hi, I am observing an issue related with inclusion of time.h when generating project for NUCLEO-H753ZI with help of STM32CubeMX. attached ZIP file contains project and IOC file [lwIP_Ethernet_WORKS_03.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25109447/lwIP_Ethernet_WORKS_03.zip) I initially thought it to be an issue with LWIP related code, but later figured out that the problem reported in the file STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.12.1\Middlewares\Third_Party\LwIP\system\arch\cc.h is because of below conditional compilation which should work for Keil AC5 but will not work for Keil AC6 #if defined (__GNUC__) & !defined (__CC_ARM) #define LWIP_TIMEVAL_PRIVATE 0 #include <sys/time.h> #endif and possibly need to be updated to: #if defined (__GNUC__) & !( defined(__CC_ARM) /* Arm Compiler 5 */ || ( defined(__ARMCC_VERSION) && (__ARMCC_VERSION >= 6010000) /* Arm Compiler 6 (armclang) */ ) ) #define LWIP_TIMEVAL_PRIVATE 0 #include <sys/time.h> #endif May you please help resolve the concern. The above fix may cause other issues to pop up, which shall also need fix within ethernetif.c Thanks, Rajeev

Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H743ZI, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=327

Fix: **Describe the set-up** The example was ported to our custom board with STM32H735V and there I discovered the bugs.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H743ZI, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, STM32H735V, IDE, SCB_EnableICache, EE_VerifyPageFullWriteVariable, EEPROM

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** The example was ported to our custom board with STM32H735V and there I discovered the bugs. IDE used is STM32CubeIDE version 1.19.0. **Describe the bug** 1. As mentioned [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/309#issuecomment-3025018673), there are missing calls to SCB_EnableICache() before exit points in EE_VerifyPageFullWriteVariable(). https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L617-L645 Instruction cache then may end up disabled forever. 2. EE_VerifyPageFullyErased() - if really the whole sector is to be checked, either increments have to be 2-byte or dereferenced value be uint32_t (four bytes). I prefer the former since the value is checked against ERASED which is uint16_t. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L341-L360 My solution is that EndAddress = (uint32_t)(Address + (PAGE_SIZE - 2U)); and increment Address = Address + 2;. 3. EE_VerifyPageFullWriteVariable() does not actually check if all the bytes are set to 0xFFFFFFFF. Since there are two 32-byte writes, actually 16 32-bit words should be checked for 0xFFFFFFFF. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L622-L634 The code actually checks only the first word. My fix was along the lines of if (is_flashword_erased(Address) && is_flashword_erased(Address + 32)) with static inline int is_flashword_erased(uint32_t addr) { for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) { if (*((__IO uint32_t*)(addr + i*4)) != 0xFFFFFFFFU) return 0; } return 1; } 4. This is the gravest one that I think actually caused our problems. It consists of three parts: a. Wrong offset in EE_Init() initial check for detecting the variable. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L137 Where does the value 6 come from? I think that the correct should be 128 - 64 for the header and 64 for the address offset. So actually if (( *(__IO uint16_t*)(PAGE0_BASE_ADDRESS + PAGE_HEADER_SIZE + EE_ADDRESS_OFFSET)) == VirtAddVarTab[VarIdx]) where PAGE_HEADER_SIZE is 64 and EE_ADDRESS_OFFSET is 64. b. Wrong stopping address in EE_ReadVariable() - the last check goes to the page header. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L398. I think that the correct code is while (Address >= (PageStartAddress + PAGE_HEADER_SIZE)) or maybe just > since the first four-word actually contains the variable value. c. EE_VerifyPageFullWriteVariable() start address - this is the main problem https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/8bc11985e1ffb47ab74bac67d20e48fa26038dd3/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L612 The check actually starts at the sector beginning which should contain the page header. Even though it should not be erased if it is a valid page, this ends up colliding with the header after some time. I think that the correct start address should be Address = (uint32_t)(EEPROM_START_ADDRESS + (uint32_t)(ValidPage * PAGE_SIZE) + PAGE_HEADER_SIZE); **How To Reproduce** With intensive writing, I always end up with both pages containing data with the page header inconsistent which in turn results in deleting of one of the pages and missing data. I think that it was caused by the point 4. which caused header invalidation and subsequent data inconsistency. With the fixes the code now seems to be running reliably. **Aditional Context** Again, also relevant to STM32H743I-EVAL. Not sure for NUCLEO-H7A3ZI-Q, maybe all the offsets I introduce should be halved since the writes are half the size.

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 219313 Hello @khevessy, Thank you for your report. Regarding point 4 that you mentioned, I am unable to identify any issues with the current implementation. Could you please provide more details or clarify the specific problem you are experiencing? Page header has 2 bytes at the beginning (receive data / valid page), then there are 30 zero bytes from the 32 byte write. Since EE_VerifyPageFullWriteVariable() increases the address by 64 when searching the erased words, there are also 32 empty bytes, that's why I say that the header is 64 bytes in total. 4a. IIUC, code tries directly checking the first variable saved in the memory. However, dereferencing PAGE0_BASE_ADDRESS + 6 goes into page header. 4b. Search for the variable to read goes into the page header in the last iteration. 4c. Search for erased address for write of the variable starts at the page beginning which is occupied by the page header. The variable can never be written there. With only points from 4., I am now unable to reproduce the issue with invalid header, it was probably caused by some combination of the mentioned issues since I was fixing them step by step. Hello @khevessy, Sorry

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: STM32H7 USB PCD driver calls CDC transmission in the interrupt, causing communication interruption
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H723, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=322
Root cause: Hello @tangb765, It looks there is a problem with the way you are clearing the TIM's flag.
Fix: **Caution** When a high-priority timer frequently sends large data packets, interrupt preemption may occur.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H723, HAL, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, HAL_PCD_IRQHandler, CDC_Transmit_HS, CDC, ScanA_Init

Technical details:
**Caution** When a high-priority timer frequently sends large data packets, interrupt preemption may occur. This leads to the scenario where after the function HAL_PCD_IRQHandler() executes hcdc->TxState = 0U, the timer interrupt calls CDC_Transmit_HS to send data. At this point, there might be an abnormal clearing of the status flag, resulting in transmission failure? **Describe the set-up** STM32H723 development board with USB interface **Describe the bug** After running for some time, the STM32H723 development board (with USB HS interface) fails to send data to the PC via USB CDC. **Additional context** void ScanA_Init(void) { TIM_HandleTypeDef htim13={0}; __HAL_RCC_TIM13_CLK_ENABLE(); htim13.Instance = TIM13; htim13.Init.Prescaler = 0; htim13.Init.CounterMode = TIM_COUNTERMODE_UP; htim13.Init.Period = 16999; htim13.Init.ClockDivision = TIM_CLOCKDIVISION_DIV1; htim13.Init.RepetitionCounter = 0; htim13.Init.AutoReloadPreload = TIM_AUTORELOAD_PRELOAD_DISABLE; if (HAL_TIM_Base_Init(&htim13) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } HAL_NVIC_SetPriority(TIM8_UP_TIM13_IRQn, 0, 0); HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ(TIM8_UP_TIM13_IRQn); AL_TIM_Base_Start_IT(&htim13); } void TIM8_UP_TIM13_IRQHandler(void) { if ((TIM13->SR & TIM_FLAG_UPDATE)== TIM_FLAG_UPDATE) { TIM13->SR = ~(TIM_FLAG_UPDATE); USB_printf(">>>\r\n%s\r\n",a_large_1024byte_str); } } **Bug fix method – please help verify correctness?** @ stm32h7xx_hal_pcd.c line: 1216 #if (USE_HAL_PCD_REGISTER_CALLBACKS == 1U) hpcd->DataInStageCallback(hpcd, (uint8_t)epnum); #else HAL_PCD_DataInStageCallback(hpcd, (uint8_t)epnum); #endif /* USE_HAL_PCD_REGISTER_CALLBACKS */ **return;**

Key comments:
Hello @tangb765, It looks there is a problem with the way you are clearing the TIM's flag. You are using the assignment operator =, while, I guess, you intend to do a **bitwise operation** using the &= operator as shown below. diff void TIM8_UP_TIM13_IRQHandler(void) { if ((TIM13->SR & TIM_FLAG_UPDATE)== TIM_FLAG_UPDATE) { - TIM13->SR = ~(TIM_FLAG_UPDATE); + TIM13->SR &= ~(TIM_FLAG_UPDATE); USB_printf(">>>\r\n%s\r\n",a_large_1024byte_str); } } Could this be the origin of the problem? Moreover, it is advised to configure **the USB with a higher priority than the TIM**. Otherwise, and since USB operations are mainly based on interrupts, calling a USB operation from a TIM ISR is likely to result in some kind of **priority inversion** situation. I hope this helps. Please let me know whether this solves your issue. Dear, @ALABSTM Thank you for your response. 1、Yes, TIM13->SR = ~(TIM_FLAG_UPDATE) is a coding error. After fixing it, there was no improvement. 2、The interrupt priority of USB cannot be set to the highest (as other peripheral interrupts require the highest priority). issues.issue_title: Add CMake Support
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Add CMake Support
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=high, evidence_strength=low, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=316
Root cause: Here is a high-level overview of the CMake infrastructure being considered: !
Fix: # Overview I’d like to contribute CMake integration for this repository, enabling projects that use CMake to easily consume it as a dependency.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, Middleware, USB, configuration_help, high, enhancement, wontfix, projects, find_package, FetchContent_Declare, GIT_REPOSITORY, GIT_TAG

Technical details:
# Overview I’d like to contribute CMake integration for this repository, enabling projects that use CMake to easily consume it as a dependency. # Proposal ## Find Package Support Add support to allow this repository to be discovered via CMake’s find_package() command. This involves providing a Find<package>.cmake module file, where <package> is a name representing this repository. For example: FindSTM32CubeH7.cmake. ## Usage ### Fetching the Repository Consuming projects would include the following in their CMake configuration: cmake FetchContent_Declare( stm32cubeH7 GIT_REPOSITORY git@github.com:STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7.git GIT_TAG v1.12.1 GIT_SUBMODULES_RECURSE TRUE GIT_PROGRESS TRUE ) FetchContent_MakeAvailable(stm32cubeH7) list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH ${stm32cubeH7_SOURCE_DIR}) This fetches the repository (including submodules) into the CMake build directory. The CMAKE_MODULE_PATH is then updated to include the repository path, so CMake can find the custom FindSTM32CubeH7.cmake file during find_package() calls. ### Finding the Package Once fetched, the consuming project would locate and request specific components using: cmake find_package( STM32CubeH7 COMPONENTS rcc gpio i2c usb_hid_device REQUIRED ) This locates FindSTM32CubeH7.cmake and triggers additional includes for CMake files within this repository that manage locating source files for the requested components. In the example above, the consuming project requests the rcc, gpio, i2c, and usb_hid_device drivers. The added CMake support will identify the relevant source files and configure them into a library for the consuming project. ### Linking Finally, the consuming project would link against the created library using: cmake target_link_libraries(<target> PRIVATE stm32cubeh7) Where <target> is the name of the executable or library target defined by the consuming project via add_executable() or add_library(). # Summary This proposal improves CMake interoperability for this repository, making it easier to integrate into modern, CMake-based embedded projects via standard tooling like FetchContent and find_package().

issues.issue_title: BDMA should check for memory addresses at transfer start
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: BDMA should check for memory addresses at transfer start
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H743VI, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=other, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=315
Root cause: Hello @giuliomoro, Thank you for the report, and I apologize for the delayed response.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * STM32H743VI custom board * STM32CubeIDE **Additional context** Via CubeMx, I set up I2C4 as master with DMA for Rx only, NVIC enabled for I2C4 event, I2C4 error, BDMA channel 0 global.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H743VI, HAL, DMA, high, enhancement, wontfix, NVIC, BDMA, HAL_I2C_Master_Receive_DMA, HAL_I2C_MasterRxCpltCallback, HAL_I2C_ErrorCallback

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * STM32H743VI custom board * STM32CubeIDE **Additional context** Via CubeMx, I set up I2C4 as master with DMA for Rx only, NVIC enabled for I2C4 event, I2C4 error, BDMA channel 0 global. In the code, I start the transaction with HAL_I2C_Master_Receive_DMA(&hi2c4, address << 1, gI2cDmaRecv, gI2cDmaRecvSize); Neither HAL_I2C_MasterRxCpltCallback() nor HAL_I2C_ErrorCallback() are ever called. BDMA_Channel0_IRQHandler() is called and in turn it calls HAL_DMA_IRQHandler() and hdma->XferCallback (i.e.: I2C_DMAError()) but I see no user-defined callbacks being called. HAL_DMA_GetError(hdma) returns HAL_DMA_ERROR_TE. As a matter of fact, the transfer error is due to the target memory(gI2cDmaRecv) not being in the RAM_D3 block. My bad, I fixed that and it works. Still, I see are two issues with the current approach: - [ ] Detect errors at initialisation: when calling HAL_I2C_Master_Receive_DMA(), the HAL should check that the source and target addresses are valid for the type of DMA in use on the specific platform, insofar as possible. In this case, if using BDMA it should know that the destination buffer (pointer and size) should be in SRAM domain D3. If it's not, it should fail at initialisation and return a meaningful error. - [ ] Call error callback if errors are encountered after initialisation: if an error is encountered by the DMA at runtime, HAL_I2C_ErrorCallback() should probably be called? I am not the only one confused by this behaviour ([see](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-products/stm32h7-s-i2c4-using-bdma-not-triggering-complete-callbacks/td-p/53004/page/2))

Key comments:
Hello @giuliomoro, Thank you for the report, and I apologize for the delayed response. I have analyzed the issue and checked with our team, and you are indeed right about the request. Unfortunately, there are currently no plans to implement this check, but I will keep you updated if anything changes. Please, allow me to close the issue and thank you for understanding.

Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=308
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 202361 Hi @timschuerewegen, You point looks relevant.
Fix: I am using STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, Middleware, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, mw, MSC, usbd_msc_scsi, LUN, SCSI

Technical details:
I am using STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.11.2 and found a bug in \Middlewares\ST\STM32_USB_Device_Library\Class\MSC\Src\usbd_msc_scsi.c that can cause read/write errors when using multiple luns of different sizes. This is what happened ... I was unable to open a text file on the LUN 0 drive after Windows had detected the LUN 0 and 1 drives. I used WireShark and saw the following: ... SCSI: Test Unit Ready LUN: 0x00 SCSI: Response LUN: 0x00 (Test Unit Ready) (Good) SCSI: Test Unit Ready LUN: 0x01 SCSI: Response LUN: 0x01 (Test Unit Ready) (Good) SCSI: Read(10) LUN: 0x00 (LBA: 0x00587bf0, Len: 1) SCSI: Response LUN: 0x00 (Read(10)) (Check Condition) with Status: Command Failed (0x01) ... I put several breakpoints in the SCSI_Read10 function and saw that SCSI_CheckAddressRange was failing because the hmsc->scsi_blk_nbr variable contained the number of blocks for LUN 1, not LUN 0. The SCSI_Read10, SCSI_Read12, SCSI_Write10 and SCSI_Write12 functions are all using the hmsc->scsi_blk_size and hmsc->scsi_blk_nbr variables but those values can be wrong when using multiple luns of different sizes. Those functions should first update those values via a call to GetCapacity just like the SCSI_ReadCapacity10, SCCSI_ReadCapacity16 and SCSI_ReadFormatCapacity functions do. I added the following code to the SCSI_Read10, SCSI_Read12, SCSI_Write10 and SCSI_Write12 functions and the issue was fixed. if (((USBD_StorageTypeDef *)pdev->pUserData[pdev->classId])->GetCapacity(lun, &hmsc->scsi_blk_nbr, &hmsc->scsi_blk_size) != 0) { SCSI_SenseCode(pdev, lun, NOT_READY, MEDIUM_NOT_PRESENT); return -1; }

Technical details:
Environment: STM32H743VGT6 with Keil V5 HAL project generated by CUBEMX, the lab version is STM32Cube FW_H7 V1.12.0 Bug phenomenon: The baud rate of the USART peripheral is half as low as expected. Cause of bug(Maybe?): [STM32CubeH7](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master)/[Projects](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects)/[STM32H743I-EVAL](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/STM32H743I-EVAL)/[Templates_LL](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/STM32H743I-EVAL/Templates_LL)/[Src](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/STM32H743I-EVAL/Templates_LL/Src) /system_stm32h7xx.c The old version array D1CorePrescTable[16] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9} replaced by D1CorePrescTable[16] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9}; uint32_t HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq(void) { /* Get HCLK source and Compute PCLK1 frequency ---------------------------*/ #if defined(RCC_D2CFGR_D2PPRE2) return (HAL_RCC_GetHCLKFreq() >> ((D1CorePrescTable[(RCC->D2CFGR & RCC_D2CFGR_D2PPRE2)>> RCC_D2CFGR_D2PPRE2_Pos]) & 0x1FU)); #else return (HAL_RCC_GetHCLKFreq() >> ((D1CorePrescTable[(RCC->CDCFGR2 & RCC_CDCFGR2_CDPPRE2)>> RCC_CDCFGR2_CDPPRE2_Pos]) & 0x1FU)); #endif } The function above uses the D2PPRE2 bit of the D2CFGR register to calculate the PCLK2 frequency by looking up the D1CorePrescTable.However, since the D2PPRE2 only has 3 bits, the new D1CorePrescTable cannot return the correct right shift count. PCLK2 results in a frequency that is doubled compared to its real value. Then the baudrate calculated by the wrong input clock frequency. Bug fix(effective for us): Revert D1CorePrescTable[] to last version.

Problem: jpeg_utils.c: pure red or pure blue pixel conversion from RGB to YCbCr will result in values too large to hold in a uint8_t buffer.
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H743, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=299
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 195507 Fixed in commit: https://github.
Fix: **board** custom board developed by our company, using the STM32H743.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H743, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, utils, IDE, UTC, JPEG_ARGB_MCU_YCbCr420_ConvertBlocks, jpeg_utils, RGB

Technical details:
**board** custom board developed by our company, using the STM32H743. **IDE** STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.16.1 Build: 22882_20240916_0822 (UTC) **Describe the bug** When using the JPEG_ARGB_MCU_YCbCr420_ConvertBlocks function (and possibly also the other convert functions) in **jpeg_utils.c** to convert an RGB input buffer to YCbCr format, pixels that have a saturated (0xFF) value on either blue or red will result in a Cb or Cr value of 256, which is too large for the uint8_t buffer. Consequently, this will overflow to 0, resulting in the absence of the color instead of the saturation of it. As an example, consider the RGB Pixel = (255,0,0). calculating the crcomp value according to: c crcomp = (int32_t)(*(BLUE_CB_RED_CR_LUT + red)) + (int32_t)(*(GREEN_CR_LUT + green)) + (int32_t)(*(BLUE_CR_LUT + blue)) + 128; would result in crcomp = 128 + 0 + 0 + 128 = 256 Next, c (*(pOutAddr + JPEG_ConvertorParams.Cr_MCU_LUT[offset])) = (crcomp); would cast this to a uint8_t, resulting in: *(pOutAddr + JPEG_ConvertorParams.Cr_MCU_LUT[offset])) = 0 instead of the desired 255. **How To Reproduce** IN our project, we take an image with a camera by using the DCMI (works) , debayer & process the image to RGB (works) and eventually encode it to JPEG. We noticed that a test image from the camera had wrong colors for the pure blue and pure red strips. You can e.g. reproduce this by using the [JPEG_EncodingFromFLASH_DMA](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/STM32H747I-EVAL/Examples/JPEG/JPEG_EncodingFromFLASH_DMA) example but use a pure red RGB or RGBA image instead. The compressed image should have a greenish color instead of the expected red. root of the problem is very likely in [this part](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/d0e2e3886ee013b56082e57f48ae9bc6c34c849a/Utilities/JPEG/jpeg_utils.c#L503) of **jpeg_utils.c** (and equivalent code in other convertors): c ycomp = (int32_t)(*(RED_Y_LUT + red)) + (int32_t)(*(GREEN_Y_LUT + green)) + (int32_t)(*(BLUE_Y_LUT + blue)); cbcomp = (int32_t)(*(RED_CB_LUT + red)) + (int32_t)(*(GREEN_CB_LUT + green)) + (int32_t)(*(BLUE_CB_RED_CR_LUT + blue)) + 128; crcomp = (int32_t)(*(BLUE_CB_RED_CR_LUT + red)) + (int32_t)(*(GREEN_CR_LUT + green)) + (int32_t)(*(BLUE_CR_LUT + blue)) + 128; (*(pOutAddr + JPEG_ConvertorParams.Y_MCU_LUT[offset])) = (ycomp); (*(pOutAddr + JPEG_ConvertorParams.Cb_MCU_LUT[offset])) = (cbcomp); (*(pOutAddr + JPEG_ConvertorParams.Cr_MCU_LUT[offset])) = (crcomp); or perhaps the lookup table. I'll let ST decide where it's best to change things. Let me know if i can provide additional info, test cases or more! Thanks in advance Jeroen

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 195507 Fixed in commit: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/commit/d0847241cf3061a1ce55dab5636cfa79a267251f Thanks a lot! Cheers Jeroen

canFilterConfig.IdType = FDCAN_EXTENDED_ID; canFilterConfig.FilterType = FDCAN_FILTER_MASK; 1. receive H723B **FAIL** * FilterID2 matches the only incomming CAN ID (0x1FFFFFFF matches all 29Bit) * gobal reject all non matching CAN IDs * should be receiving since FIlterID2 matches the send ID and the global filter rejects all other CAN IDs (no others are send, so nothing left to reject) canFilterConfig.FilterID1 = own_address; // canIdentifier canFilterConfig.FilterID2 = 0x1FFFFFFF; // mask: 0 => accept all messages HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); 2. receive H723B **FAIL** * FilterID2 match all CAN IDs * gobal reject all non matching CAN IDs * should be receiving since the FilterID matches all CAN IDs and the global filter rejects all other CAN IDs (no others are send, so nothing left to reject) canFilterConfig.FilterID1 = own_address; // canIdentifier canFilterConfig.FilterID2 = 0; // mask: 0 => accept all messages HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); 3. receive H723B **OK** * FilterID2 matches the only incomming CAN ID (0x1FFFFFFF matches all 29Bit) * gobal accept all non matching CAN IDs * receives since all IDs are allowed by global filter canFilterConfig.FilterID1 = own_address; // canIdentifier canFilterConfig.FilterID2 = 0x1FFFFFFF; // mask: 0 => accept all messages HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); 4. receive H723B **OK** FilterID2 matches the all incomming CAN IDs gobal accept all non matching CAN IDs receives since all ID are allowed by FilterID2 and by global filter canFilterConfig.FilterID1 = own_address; // canIdentifier canFilterConfig.FilterID2 = 0; // mask: 0 => accept all messages HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); Not calling HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter() at all will lead to no received message. In my understanding 1. and 2. should receive too. I seems like either the FilterID2 is set false, or that FDCAN_REJECT recjects always, despite any FilterID2 setting. **Testproject** Attached is a test project using 2 NUCLEO-144-H723 boards using FDCAN2, where H723A is the sender and H723B is the receiver. The sender will send an extended FDCAN message every second, indicated by the RED on-board LED toggling. Every successful received extended FDCAN message at the receiver will be indicated by a toggled GREEN on-board LED. Both H723A/B use the same project code, two #defines select the task. **Setup the sender H723A** uncomment line 105 at the main.c #define sender // use this definition for the sender H723A compile, program and run. The receiver will use the following global CAN filter setup // EITHER uncomment this and GREEN BOARD LED toggles -> receiving HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_ACCEPT_IN_RX_FIFO1, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); 2. setup for unsuccessful receiving comment out line 188 at the ProcessCAN.c //#define RECEIVE_SUCCSEFUL compile, program and run. The receiver will use the following global CAN filter setup, which should allow the message to pass the filter, but it doesn't. // OR uncomment this and GREEN BOARD LED does not toggle -> not receiving HAL_FDCAN_ConfigGlobalFilter(&hfdcan2, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_REJECT, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE, FDCAN_FILTER_REMOTE); [NUCLEO - H723 - FDCAN - Test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15837081/NUCLEO.-.H723.-.FDCAN.-.Test.zip)

Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=289

Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, i2c, HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady, NACK, STOP, HAL_ERROR

Technical details:
I have found a bug in the HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady function in version 1.11.3 fec141c. The problem is in the function [HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/fec141ce999da655a48e1a15db83a72d564a1312/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c#L3251) on [Line 3332](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/fec141ce999da655a48e1a15db83a72d564a1312/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c#L3332). There is a call to the [I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/fec141ce999da655a48e1a15db83a72d564a1312/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c#L6947) function . There is a new test for [I2C_IsErrorOccurred](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/blob/fec141ce999da655a48e1a15db83a72d564a1312/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c#L7143) and if so (the device is not ready and sent NACK), I2C_IsErrorOccurred waits for STOP and returns HAL_ERROR to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout. I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout returns HAL_ERROR to HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady and it immediately returns HAL_ERROR to the upcoming function without considering the number of Trials from the function parameter. **How To Reproduce** 1. Write a data block into the EEPROM using the HAL_I2C_Mem_Write function 2. Call HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady with the Trials parameter set to 1000 3. HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady return value is HAL_ERROR, only one busy test is performed Version 1.11.2 - multiple attempts to test if the device is ready (not busy) [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Logic analyzer screenshot showing an I2C transaction on STM32. Channel 1 (I2C-SDA) and Channel 0 (I2C-SCL) are displayed with repeated polling attempts after a memory write ends. A red annotation “HAL_I2C_Mem_Write END” points to the transition, followed by multiple repeated “HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady” attempts. The decoded bus annotations show repeated “Write [0x50] + NAK” responses, indicating the device at address 0x50 is not acknowledging during readiness polling. This visually supports an I2C readiness/polling issue in the HAL implementation. [IMAGE TEXT] D1 Channel 1

The trace shows repeated write attempts to address 0x50, many of them followed by NAK and the analyzer marked “Busy” in red during each retry window. Near the later part of the capture, the target begins returning ACK, the state changes to “Ready,” and the trace then proceeds into “Next data block ->” with subsequent ACKed bytes (including 0x18, 0x40, 0x00). This visually supports a device-ready polling sequence where readiness is detected only after multiple failed attempts, consistent with a HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady behavior issue. So this should be passed to the STM32CubeMX team to fix as I have noticed there are many posts from people all having related problems to the Timeout issue here Hi @AnthonyGBES, Thank you for all these helpful details. However, I generated a project using the same configuration as you described and noticed no issue. I used version **6.10.0** of CubeMX and version **1.11.2** of the STM32CubeH7 firmware. Would you mind double-checking please? Otherwise, please let me know in case I missed somehting. issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Wrong implementation of HAL_RCC_GetSysClockFreq, LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq as well as SystemCoreClockUpdate in the examples
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=284
Root cause: Hello @cryptic-quasar, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Setup** - Board: Nucleo H743ZI **Issue** I encountered a problem setting the UART baud rate using LL_RCC_GetUSARTClockFreq(LL_RCC_USART16_CLKSOURCE) as the second argument of LL_USART_SetBaudRate.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, UART, LL_RCC_GetUSARTClockFreq, LL_RCC_USART16_CLKSOURCE, LL_USART_SetBaudRate

Technical details:
**Setup** - Board: Nucleo H743ZI **Issue** I encountered a problem setting the UART baud rate using LL_RCC_GetUSARTClockFreq(LL_RCC_USART16_CLKSOURCE) as the second argument of LL_USART_SetBaudRate. The data received on my PC using the USB-to-Serial adapter were bogus. After spending hours, I finally spotted the issue and it turns out that the SystemCoreClock calculations in HAL and LL are wrong. The PLLM coefficient can only take values from 0 to 63 with 0 meaning division by 1, 1 meaning division by 2, 2 meaning division by 3, etc. The problem is that the methods I mentioned before do not take the increment of PLLM into account for the dynamic calculation of SystemCoreClock. The following is taken from stm32h7xx_hal_rcc.c: pllm = ((RCC->PLLCKSELR & RCC_PLLCKSELR_DIVM1) >> 4) ; where it must be: pllm = ((RCC->PLLCKSELR & RCC_PLLCKSELR_DIVM1) >> 4) + 1;

Key comments:
Hello @cryptic-quasar, Thank you for this report. As indicated in the RM0433 (section 8.7.11 page 398) see screenshot below the prescaler for PLLM can take values from 0 to 63 this is correct but the value 0 indicates that the prescaler is disabled. I don't see any need to add the +1 in the PLLM calculation. For the moment I didn't see the problem, may be I forgot some details. Could you please share with me more details about your issue. Tasnim [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Screenshot of a documentation excerpt describing the RCC PLL1 prescaler field DIVM1[5:0] in a register bitfield table. It explains that bits 9:4 control the prescaler for PLL1, that software can set/clear the field, and that hardware prevents modification when PLL1 is enabled (PLL1ON = 1). It also notes that DIVM1 should be set to 0 when PLL1 is not used to save power. Several encoded values are listed, with the first two lines highlighted in yellow: 000000 = prescaler disabled, 000001 = division by 1 (bypass), followed by 000010 = division by 2, 000011 = division by 3, an ellipsis for omitted values, 100000 = division by 32 (default after reset), another ellipsis, and 111111 = division by 63. [IMAGE TEXT] Bits 9:4 DIVM1[5:0]: Prescaler for PLL1
Set and cleared by software to configure the prescaler of the PLL1.
The hardware does not allow any modification of this prescaler when PLL1 is enabled (PLL1ON =
'1').
In order to save power when PLL1 is not used, the value of DIVM1 must be set to '0'.
000000: prescaler disabled
000001: division by 1 (bypass)
000010: division by 2
000011: division by 3
...
100000: division by 32 (default after reset)
...
111111: division by 63

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Using STM32CubeIDE 1.14.0 and FW)H& V1.11.1 **Describe the bug** When you generate a project for the STM32H725 using FreeRTOS and setting the Timbase Source to TIM6 it generates a completely empty ISR for TIM6. /** * @brief This function handles TIM6 global interrupt, DAC1_CH1 and DAC1_CH2 underrun error interrupts. */ void TIM6_DAC_IRQHandler(void) { /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */ /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */ /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */ /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */ } When you do the same for a H723 it generates the correct code as below, which is what should also be generated for the H725. /** * @brief This function handles TIM6 global interrupt, DAC1_CH1 and DAC1_CH2 underrun error interrupts. */ void TIM6_DAC_IRQHandler(void) { /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */ /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */ HAL_TIM_IRQHandler(&htim6); /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */ /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */ } **How To Reproduce** Create a project using an H725, enable FreeRTOS and set the timebase source to TIM6 and generate the project. Look at the ISR routine in stm32h7xx_it.c and you will see the ISR is missing the call to HAL_TIM_IRQHandler.

Key comments:
Hello @Makin-Things, First we would like to thank you for your report. We tried to reproduce the problem you described for STM32H725 using STM32CubeMX v6.10.0 with no success. Could you please check another time with the same version as me and tell me if the problem persists. @TOUNSTM thanks for your response. MSv41921V1 Therefore, I configured PC3_C as a GPIO pin using CubeMX -- [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Request Timeout Subsequently, I generated the code using CubeMX -- c gpio.c void MX_GPIO_Init(void) { GPIO_InitTypeDef GPIO_InitStruct = {0}; /* GPIO Ports Clock Enable */ __HAL_RCC_GPIOB_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOA_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOG_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOC_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOD_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOF_CLK_ENABLE(); __HAL_RCC_GPIOH_CLK_ENABLE(); /*Configure GPIO pin Output Level */ // config other pins ... /*Configure GPIO pin Output Level */ HAL_GPIO_WritePin(GPIOC, GPIO_PIN_3, GPIO_PIN_RESET); // config other pins ... /*Configure GPIO pin : PC3 */ GPIO_InitStruct.Pin = GPIO_PIN_3; GPIO_InitStruct.Mode = GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT_PP; GPIO_InitStruct.Pull = GPIO_NOPULL; GPIO_InitStruct.Speed = GPIO_SPEED_FREQ_HIGH; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOC, &GPIO_InitStruct); } However, when running the code, I found that the PC3_C pin provides no output. Then I executed the code with a debugger and inspected the configuration registers. I discovered that SYSCFG_PMCR was set to 0x0F000000 (PC3SO=1), indicating that PC3_C was not connected to PC3. The problem as addressed by modifying the PC3SO bit to 0, as depicted in the figure below. Additionally, similar pins such as PA0_C, PA1_C encountered the same problem. [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Screenshot of a register browser/property grid for STM32 SYSCFG_PMCR. The PMCR register is selected and shows value 0x07000000. Most feature bits such as I2C1FMP, I2C2FMP, I2C3FMP, I2C4FMP, PB6FMP, PB7FMP, PB8FMP, PB9FMP, and BOOSTE are unchecked. EPIS displays 0x00. The pin source selection bits show PA0SO, PA1SO, and PC2SO checked, while PC3SO is unchecked. The visual supports the issue context that the SYSCFG_PMCR configuration may be set incorrectly when configuring pins like PC3 as GPIO. [IMAGE TEXT] Property\nValue\nPMCR\n0x07000000\nI2C1FMP\nI2C2FMP\nI2C3FMP\nI2C4FMP\nPB6FMP\nPB7FMP\nPB8FMP\nPB9FMP\nBOOSTE\nEPIS\n0x00\nPA0SO\nPA1SO\nPC2SO\nPC3SO To ensure a permanent solution, I appended code at the end of the function -- c gpio.c void MX_GPIO_Init(void) { // other code ... /*Configure GPIO pin : PC3 */ GPIO_InitStruct.Pin = GPIO_PIN_3; GPIO_InitStruct.Mode = GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT_PP; GPIO_InitStruct.Pull = GPIO_NOPULL; GPIO_InitStruct.Speed = GPIO_SPEED_FREQ_HIGH; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOC, &GPIO_InitStruct); HAL_SYSCFG_AnalogSwitchConfig(SYSCFG_SWITCH_PC3, SYSCFG_SWITCH_PC3_CLOSE); } Testing has proven that the PC3_C output correctly as the behavior of PC3. Upon careful examination of CubeMX's graphical user interface, I was unable to locate any information regarding the configuration of SYSCFG_PMCR or its equivalent. Therefore, I suspect that may be a bug within the MPU Package code.

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** I'm using a H7B3 on a custom board. On this board I want to use USB with Azure USBx. The USB configuration in CubeMX is: - USB host only - DMA enabled - internal PHY - Speed: FullSpeed I'm using CubeIDE 1.10.1. The USB device I want to use with the USB Host is a Prolific-Device. **Describe the bug** Regarding the Reference Guide, USB interrupts like NAK, NYET, ... should be handled automatically by the DMA. But when I use the confguration above the interrupts never get disabled in USB_HC_StartXfer. And the interrupts get fired very often and have a huge influence on the performance of the controller. **How To Reproduce** 1. Set a breakpoint into the function USB_HC_StartXfer. 2. Connect a prolific device 3. Step through function USBx_HC((uint32_t)ch_num)->HCINTMSK &= ~(USB_OTG_HCINTMSK_NYET | USB_OTG_HCINTMSK_ACKM | USB_OTG_HCINTMSK_NAKM); 4. The code block above gets neve reached because of this check here: if (((USBx->CID & (0x1U << 8)) != 0U) && (hc->speed == USBH_HS_SPEED)) **Additional context** It has to do with this issue here: https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-products/stm32f4-stm32f7-usb-host-core-interrupt-flood/td-p/436225 But the interrupts still get triggered even when DMA is enabled **Screenshots** If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32F723, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=274
Root cause: To replicate the problem quicker set bInterval parameter to 0x1 on CDC and HID interface.
Fix: **Brief description** A serious problem with USB composite CDC-CustomHID device working reliably.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32F723, Middleware, USB, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, CDC-, HID, CDC

Technical details:
**Brief description** A serious problem with USB composite CDC-CustomHID device working reliably. I have ported your H7 Composite Custom HID - CDC example code to STM32F723 MCU. HID interface either hangs, sometimes CDC I/F hangs or data integrity fails when running loopback test on both interfaces at the same time from two different host processes. **Describe the set-up** The board: Not applicable. I was testing with STM32F723-DISCO development board. IDE: System Workbench for STM32 Observed on Windows 7, 8.1, 10 **Describe the bug** I have implemented USB composite CDC- and Custom HID device based on your H7 Composite Custom HID - CDC example code. HID I/F receives 64 bytes long reports and sends the same reports back to the host running a HID loopback test process . CDC I/F receives random bytes long packets from length between 1 to 12345 bytes and sends the same data back to the host running loopback test on the same host, however in a different process. Device enumerates OK with VID 0x483 and PID 0x5741, If I run test on one interface only it works reliably 247 without any problem. Once I run loopback test on both interfaces one of the interfaces hangs or incorrect data is received by the host. Does not matter if the code is running in HS or FS mode. For simplicity no UART is implemented on CDC side. There is just a simple loopback. The main loop is not stuck, blinking LED process is still blinking, however processing of comms on USB either CDC or HID is stuck. Looks to me like missing an interrupt processing. Minimal version of the code is in the attachment. [cdc-hid-min.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/12553923/cdc-hid-min.zip)

Key comments:
To replicate the problem quicker set bInterval parameter to 0x1 on CDC and HID interface. in usbd_customhid.h #define CUSTOM_HID_HS_BINTERVAL 0x1U #define CUSTOM_HID_FS_BINTERVAL 0x1U in usbd_cdc.h #define CDC_HS_BINTERVAL 0x1U #define CDC_FS_BINTERVAL 0x1U HI there, please is anyone looking at the issue. We need to sort this out asap. Hi @danielsulik, Our apology for this delayed reply. Your report has been forwarded to our development teams for investigation. I will keep you informed. Hi @danielsulik, By the way, **STM32CubeF7** firmware still supports version 2.11.0 of the USB Device library, while the **latest version** is 2.11.2 including some fixes. Would you give it a try? You can find it [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32_mw_usb_device) and could easily integrate it manually into your project. Hi @danielsulik, Are you still facing the same issue? Your report has been forwarded to our development teams. Let's wait for their feedback. ST Internal Reference: 184861 Yes, still the same problem. Regards Daniel From: Ali LABBENE ***@***.***> Sent: Monday

issues.issue_title: HAL_UART_Transmit can generate faulty error
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_UART_Transmit can generate faulty error
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=272
Root cause: Hello @ra1u, Thank you for this report.
Fix: Function [HAL_UART_Transmit()](https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, needs clarification, HAL_UART_Transmit, HAL_TIMEOUT, UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout

Technical details:
Function [HAL_UART_Transmit()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/91d4c89228e766a968f8daebc78eb7143d95184e/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L1120) can return HAL_TIMEOUT error that should not be returned. Issue is that HAL_UART_Transmit() uses [UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/91d4c89228e766a968f8daebc78eb7143d95184e/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L3414) In case that there is rx timeout (data was regularly received during transmission and rx timout isr is raised) [HAL_TIMEOUT](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/91d4c89228e766a968f8daebc78eb7143d95184e/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L3463) is returned during transmission.

Key comments:
Hello @ra1u, Thank you for this report. We will get back to you as soon as we analyze it further. This may take some time. Thank you for your comprehension. Hi @ra1u, Would it be possible to share the whole project you have used to reproduce the issue in order to allow a better analysis of the problem. I am sorry I cant share project, but out of my head it should be following. // config Config uart set rx timeouts -> HAL_UART_ReceiverTimeout_Config(UART_HandleTypeDef *huart, uint32_t TimeoutValue) enable rx timeout -> HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_UART_EnableReceiverTimeout(UART_HandleTypeDef *huart) In our case we use customised uart ISR handler, however issue remains. We would expect, that timeouts for RX and TX are to be handled separately and that Rx timeout does not trigger error in UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout() when waiting for TX to complete. Our internal patch for this is that we added additional argument for UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout that distinguish direction. (it is equivalent as replacing UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout with two functions UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout_RX and UART_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout_TX ) Hello @ra1u, Just to be sure, in your project you used HAL_UART

issues.issue_title: VECT_TAB_OFFSET comments in different releases
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: VECT_TAB_OFFSET comments in different releases
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=268
Root cause: Hello @escherstair, Thank you for this report.
Fix: In file system_stm32h7xx.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, usage_question, high, question, cmsis, system_stm32h7xx, VECT_TAB_OFFSET, VECT_TAB_BASE_ADDRESS

Technical details:
In file system_stm32h7xx.c the macro VECT_TAB_OFFSET is defined in different ways under several conditions. This is ok. But I see a comments on these definition, that changes from release to release, and I don't understand why. You can see it blaming the file [system_stm32h7xx.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blame/master/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32H7xx/Source/Templates/system_stm32h7xx.c). In release 1.9.1 it was #define VECT_TAB_OFFSET 0x00000000U /*!< Vector Table base offset field. This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */ note the value 0x200 In release 1.10.0 it was #define VECT_TAB_OFFSET 0x00000000U /*!< Vector Table base offset field. This value must be a multiple of 0x300. */ note that now the value is 0x300 In release 1.11.0 it is #define VECT_TAB_OFFSET 0x00000000U /*!< Vector Table base offset field. This value must be a multiple of 0x400. */ note the value 0x400 I dont' understand the reason for this change. Similar changes in the comment can be seen for VECT_TAB_BASE_ADDRESS I need to relocate the vector table, and so I must be sure which is the allowed values. And most importan idf they change with releases on the firmware. I have an application developed with 1.9.1 and my offset is a multiple of 0x200 (but not a multiple of 0x400) Should I change it to a different value (multiple of 0x400) if I migrate my project to firmware 1.11.0?

Key comments:
Hello @escherstair, Thank you for this report. We will get back to you as soon as we analyze it further. This may take some time. Thank you for your comprehension. Please check this too https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/issues/2 Hi, @escherstair, the offset multiple to consider is 0x400 indeed. As suggested by @carlo-dev-git, the confirmation can be found in issue [cmsis_device_h7#2](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/issues/2#issuecomment-1094765954). The rationale is that the vector table offset shall: * be a multiple of its total size in bytes **rounded to the nearest** power of 2, * comply to the constraint that **bits 0 to 8 of the VTOR** register are reserved, thus shall be **left to zero**. As for STM32H7, we have 162 lines + 16 exceptions = (162 + 16) x 4 = 0x2C8 --> rounded to 0x400. You may find further details in the [programmers manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/programming_manual/pm0253-stm32f7-series-and-stm32h7-series-cortexm7-processor-programming-manual-stmicroelectronics.pdf), revision 5, page 197, paragraph 4.3.4. I hope this answers your question. Please allow me to close this thread. **PS:** @carlo-dev-git,

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * NUCLEO-H723ZG NUH723ZG$AT2 * STM32CubeIDE v1.12.1 **Describe the bug** In the function USBH_MSC_BOT_Process from file Middlewares\ST\STM32_USB_Host_Library\Class\MSC\Src\usbh_msc_bot.c the length of sent data may be too long in some case. case BOT_DATA_OUT: (void)USBH_BulkSendData(phost, MSC_Handle->hbot.pbuf, MSC_Handle->OutEpSize, MSC_Handle->OutPipe, 1U); MSC_Handle->hbot.state = BOT_DATA_OUT_WAIT; break; With a custom SCSI device, the command is misunderstood and the device never respond because we are sending 64 bytes instead of 36 expected in the variable MSC_Handle->hbot.cbw.field.DataTransferLength. **How To Reproduce** Use the USBH_StatusTypeDef USBH_MSC_BOT_Process(USBH_HandleTypeDef *phost, uint8_t lun) function. **Additional context** My way to fix this is to modify function to this: case BOT_DATA_OUT: (void)USBH_BulkSendData(phost, MSC_Handle->hbot.pbuf, (MSC_Handle->hbot.cbw.field.DataTransferLength > MSC_Handle->OutEpSize) ? MSC_Handle->OutEpSize : MSC_Handle->hbot.cbw.field.DataTransferLength, MSC_Handle->OutPipe, 1U); MSC_Handle->hbot.state = BOT_DATA_OUT_WAIT; break;

issues.issue_title: USB_Host driver: potential buffer overflow when parsing configuration descriptor
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USB_Host driver: potential buffer overflow when parsing configuration descriptor
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H743I, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=262
Root cause: I found this issue has been revised (CVE-2021-42553).
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Board: stm32h743i-eval **Describe the bug** In source file [usblctreq.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H743I, Middleware, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, mw, usbh_ctlreq, USBH_ParseCfgDesc, ep_ix, USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Board: stm32h743i-eval **Describe the bug** In source file [usblctreq.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c), the function USBH_ParseCfgDesc is responsible for parsing the configuration description of USB device. At [line 507](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L507), the number of endpoint descriptors to be parsed depends on bNumEndpoints field as shown in [line 485](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L485) and each endpoint is indexed by ep_ix. However, the driver assumes that the maximum number of endpoints per interface is 2 (defined by macro USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS). Therefore, a buffer overflow on array Ep_Desc would arise at line 507 if a malicious USB device responds more than USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS (2) endpoint descriptors (i.e., bNumEndpoints >= USBH_MAX_NUM_ENDPOINTS).

The issue you pointed out has been fixed in the frame of version **3.5.1** of our USB Host library, available [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32_mw_usb_host/tree/38bc365e09b89c43b495af7261e31fe90a07335c). Currently, the STM32CubeH7 firmware still integrates version **3.5.0** of this library. However, you can easily download the newer version and integrate it manually into your package.

Problem: I2C: Mixed transfers methods causing Interrupts to hang MCU
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H753I, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=260
Root cause: Hello @Corderbollie , Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Setup** * Board: STM32H753I-EVAL2 * STM32CubeIDE, STM32CubeMX 6.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H753I, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, STM32H753I-EVAL2, GNU, STM32, FW_H7

Technical details:
**Setup** * Board: STM32H753I-EVAL2 * STM32CubeIDE, STM32CubeMX 6.8.1 * GNU Tools for STM32 (9-2020-q2-update) * STM32Cube FW_H7 V1.11.0 * I2C1, 100 KHz, 7-Bit Address **Bug Description** A testprogramm acting as I2C Master is connected via I2C1 to a Slave. The slave emulates an EEPROM via I2C and offers 128 Byte to read/write using combined transactions (with repeated start) using the HAL_I2C_Mem_... functions. The address to read from or to write to is sent by the master as a 16-Bit value. When HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_DMA is executed as first read function from the master, then any following HAL_I2C_Mem_Write... function except the HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_DMA function will cause I2C interrupts to hang the MCU. **How To Reproduce** 1. Perform a call to HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_DMA followed by a call to HAL_I2C_Mem_Write (i.e. DMA then Polling) 2. I2C (stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c) 3. The use case is to mix different transaction methods (DMA, Interrupt, Polling) in an application and to perform e.g. Reads using DMA and writes using Interrupt. 4. Perform a call to HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_DMA followed by a call to HAL_I2C_Mem_Write (i.e. DMA then Polling) or HAL_I2C_Mem_Write_IT **Additional context** I found that after execution of HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_DMA TXIE is still enabled in the I2C 1->CR1 register. In I2C1->ISR register TXE and TXIS are set causing the interrupt to fire. However the call to HAL_I2C_Mem_Write (Polling) sets the function pointer XferISR in the I2C handle to zero and the interrupt is not handled. Upon execution of HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT after a DMA Write, the transaction hangs after the master has sent the address and one byte of the 2 byte read location (see screenshot 2) **Screenshots** Screenshot 1: Debug View with call stack and registers [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] IDE/debugger screenshot from an STM32CubeH7 embedded project (Eclipse/STM32CubeIDE style) showing a suspended thread stopped inside HAL_I2C_EV_IRQHandler in stm32h7xx_hal_i2c.c around line 4497. The call stack on the left highlights HAL_I2C_EV_IRQHandler, I2C1_EV_IRQHandler, and a signal handler, indicating an interrupt-related halt. The center editor displays the HAL I2C event and error IRQ handler code with the current execution line on flag/source reads and a call to hI2C->XferISR(hi2c, itflags, itsources). On the right, the register/bitfield view is focused on I2C1 with CR1 showing enabled interrupt sources (value 0x3), ISR showing current interrupt flags (value 0x8003), and the decoded bits with TXE and TXIS highlighted/active while other flags remain clear except BUSY. Annotations/arrows explain that interrupt sources are enabled, current interrupt flags are present, and the XferISR callback is currently set to polling rather than an ISR-specific routine, illustrating the mixed-transfer/interrupt-hang diagnosis context. issues.issue_title: H730 ADC3: macros to calculate temperature and Vref voltage
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: H730 ADC3: macros to calculate temperature and Vref voltage
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=259
Root cause: Hello @KubeckPL, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Caution** In the macros in the Low-Layer library to calculate Vref voltage and MCU internal temperature, there is an error for the H730 processor.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, ADC, usage_question, medium, question, MCU, ADC3

Technical details:
**Caution** In the macros in the Low-Layer library to calculate Vref voltage and MCU internal temperature, there is an error for the H730 processor. **__LL_ADC_CALC_VREFANALOG_VOLTAGE** https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/b75d4ea0a368c0e2e7bb9c40c1258a39fff0919a/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_ll_adc.h#L2417 **__LL_ADC_CALC_TEMPERATURE:** https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/b75d4ea0a368c0e2e7bb9c40c1258a39fff0919a/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_ll_adc.h#L2471 Both of the above macros use another macro, which is __LL_ADC_CONVERT_DATA_RESOLUTION. In this macro, an ADC resolution of 16 bits is implemented. This configuration is not correct when the user uses ADC3 to measure temperature and Vref voltage, because ADC3 is of a resolution of 12 bits. Using a macro with 16-bit scaling leads to erroneous measurement results. The __LL_ADC_CONVERT_DATA_RESOLUTION_ADC3 macro is defined in the Low-Layer library, but it is not used in any case: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/b75d4ea0a368c0e2e7bb9c40c1258a39fff0919a/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_ll_adc.h#L2359 Tools used: - STM32CubeIDE V1.12, - HAL Driver version number V1.11.1 Please analyze the problem. Best regards.

issues.issue_title: UART: No DMA Full Interrupt with DMA Receive to Idle mode
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: UART: No DMA Full Interrupt with DMA Receive to Idle mode
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7B3ZIT6, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=255
Root cause: Hi @Meravid, Indeed, the HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() is a Rx event notification called after use of advanced reception service, it is called each time a data is received.
Fix: **Caution** The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3ZIT6, HAL, DMA, usage_question, medium, question, STM32, UTC, UART, BSP, UART4_RX

Technical details:
**Caution** The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project. For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus) **Describe the set-up** * STM32H7B3ZIT6 * STM32CubeIDE * Version: 1.10.1 Build: 12716_20220707_0928 (UTC) **Describe the bug** With DMA receive to idle mode no interrupt is triggered if the DMA buffer is completely full. This means, if your DMA buffer is 100 bytes large and already 80 bytes were received the reception of additional 20 bytes will trigger no interrupt. If you would receive 19 or 21 bytes instead of 20 bytes there is one triggered. **How To Reproduce** 1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project Receiving messages with arbitrary length via UART in combination with DMA. 3. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...) The condition in Drivers\STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c is not correct. On the left side of the following screenshot the original condition is shown. On the right side is a possible bug fix shown. [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Side-by-side code diff view from a C source file in STM32 HAL UART receive-to-idle DMA handling. The visible hunk is around lines 2410–2421 and shows logic checking whether DMA mode is enabled in UART, reading the remaining DMA counter, and deciding whether to notify an IDLE event only if some data has already been received. The highlighted change appears on the conditional at line 2419, where the left and right panes compare the expression involving nb_remaining_rx_data and huart->RxXferSize. The screen is focused on the comparison area with the diff indicator across the center. [IMAGE TEXT] 2410    /* Check if DMA mode is enabled in UART */
2411    if (HAL_IS_BIT_SET(huart->Instance->CR3, USART_CR3_DMAR))
2412    {
2413      /* DMA mode enabled */
2414      /* Check received length : If all expected data are received, do nothing,
2415         (DMA cplt callback will be called).
2416         Otherwise, if at least one data has already been received, IDLE event is to be notified to user */
2417      uint16_t nb_remaining_rx_data = (uint16_t) __HAL_DMA_GET_COUNTER(huart->hdmarx);
2418      if ((nb_remaining_rx_data > 0U)
2419          && (nb_remaining_rx_data < huart->RxXferSize))
2420      {
2421        /* Reception is not complete */ 4. The use case that generates the problem Reception of UART message with DMA Receive to Idle mode, so that the DMA buffer is completely filled. 5. How we can reproduce the problem * UART4_RX DMA settings [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Screenshot of an STM32CubeMX DMA configuration panel for UART4_RX using DMA1 Stream 1, set for Peripheral to Memory direction with Low priority. The DMA Request Settings section shows Mode set to Circular, Peripheral increment address unchecked, Memory increment address checked, Use FIFO unchecked, Threshold field greyed/empty, and both Peripheral and Memory Data Width set to Byte. Burst Size fields appear disabled/empty. This configuration is consistent with UART receive-to-idle DMA setup, where circular DMA and byte-wide transfers are enabled for memory buffering. [IMAGE TEXT] UART4_RX\nDMA1 Stream 1\nPeripheral To Memory\nLow\nAdd\nDelete\nDMA Request Settings\nPeripheral\nMemory\nMode\nCircular\nIncrement Address\nUse Fifo\nThreshold\nData Width\nByte\nByte\nBurst Size * Create receive buffer of 100 bytes * Send five times a messages with 20 bytes to your device * Observe that for the last message void HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback(UART_HandleTypeDef* huart, uint16_t Size) is not called **Additional context** If you have a first analysis or patch correction, thank you to share your proposal. **Screenshots** If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

Key comments:
Hi @Meravid, Indeed, the HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() is a Rx event notification called after use of advanced reception service, it is called each time a data is received. In the case of DMA receive to idle mode, in the end of transfer the HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() is called as part of the DMA transfer complete callback. Consequently, once the DMA UART receive process is complete, the transfer complete interrupt is triggered, and UART_DMAReceiveCplt() is called which in turn calls HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() . https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ed7d3d4a8e0961ad2bcb21ba7681d5443964253c/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L3738-L3747 With regard, Hi @Meravid, Please allow me to close this thread as no activity. You may reopen it at anytime if you have any details to share with us in order to help you to solve the issue. Thank you for your comprehension.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3I, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, STM32H7B3I-DK, net_conf_es_wifi_spi, SPI_WIFI_ResetModule, HAL_GetTick

Technical details:
**Bug Description** - Tag: v1.11.0 - Buggy code: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/v1.11.0/Projects/STM32H7B3I-DK/Demonstrations/ClockAndWeather/Core/Src/net_conf_es_wifi_spi.c#L296 C static int8_t SPI_WIFI_ResetModule(void) { uint32_t tickstart = HAL_GetTick(); uint8_t Prompt[6]; uint8_t count = 0; HAL_StatusTypeDef Status; WIFI_RESET_MODULE(); WIFI_ENABLE_NSS(); SPI_WIFI_DelayUs(10); while (WIFI_IS_CMDDATA_READY()) { Status = HAL_SPI_Receive(&hspi, &Prompt[count], 1, 0xFFFF); // !!! Buggy line: bound check is missing !!! count += 2; if (((HAL_GetTick() - tickstart) > 0xFFFF) || (Status != HAL_OK)) { WIFI_DISABLE_NSS(); return -1; } } WIFI_DISABLE_NSS(); if ((Prompt[0] != 0x15) || (Prompt[1] != 0x15) || (Prompt[2] != '\r') || (Prompt[3] != '\n') || (Prompt[4] != '>') || (Prompt[5] != ' ')) { return -1; } return 0; } - Description: In function SPI_WIFI_ResetModule, it invokes HAL_SPI_Receive() to receive data from SPI interface and places the received data to array prompt at the index specified by count, then it adds count with 2. Bound check on array prompt is missing, which may cause stack buffer overflow and corrupt tickstart if count exceeds the length of prompt. **Patch Suggestion** Add bound check before invoking HAL_SPI_Receive(). C static int8_t SPI_WIFI_ResetModule(void) { uint32_t tickstart = HAL_GetTick(); uint8_t Prompt[6]; uint8_t count = 0; HAL_StatusTypeDef Status; WIFI_RESET_MODULE(); WIFI_ENABLE_NSS(); SPI_WIFI_DelayUs(10); while (WIFI_IS_CMDDATA_READY()) { // Patch: bound check before receiving data from SPI if (count == 4) { WIFI_DISABLE_NSS(); return -1; } Status = HAL_SPI_Receive(&hspi, &Prompt[count], 1, 0xFFFF); count += 2; ... } ... return 0; }

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: NUCLEO-H723ZG, LwIP_HTTP_Server_Socket_RTOS: Ethernet receive fails because DCache is not invalidated in pbuf_free_custom
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H723ZG, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=244
Root cause: I have done some further research, the combination of cache + DMA is known to be tricky.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** - NUCLEO-H723ZG - TCP Echo Server based on the application example LwIP_HTTP_Server_Socket_RTOS I am transmitting random packets of length=255 byte to the mcu and back to the pc in a endless loop.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H723ZG, HAL, ETH, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, TCP, LwIP_HTTP_Server_Socket_RTOS, pbuf_free_custom

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** - NUCLEO-H723ZG - TCP Echo Server based on the application example LwIP_HTTP_Server_Socket_RTOS I am transmitting random packets of length=255 byte to the mcu and back to the pc in a endless loop. The packet contains random data + a crc32 checksum of that data at the end. At random times, when calculating that packet checksum on the mcu, the checksums do not match. That means that the receiving of that packet failed. **Describe the bug** When the pbuf, that is free'd in the function pbuf_free_custom, is not invalidated afterwards (using SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr), 32 bytes of the old contents of that pbuf randomly appear when receiving a message in a later packet. **How To Reproduce** 1. Explicitly invalidate the contents of the freed pbuf in the function like this void pbuf_free_custom( struct pbuf* p ) { struct pbuf_custom* custom_pbuf = (struct pbuf_custom*) p; uint8_t* data = (uint8_t*) ( p->payload ); if( p->len >= 8 ) { *( data + 0 ) = 0x77; *( data + 1 ) = 0x77; *( data + 2 ) = 0x77; *( data + 3 ) = 0x77; memset( data + 4, 0x88, p->len - 8 ); *( data + ( p->len - 1 ) ) = 0x55; *( data + ( p->len - 2 ) ) = 0x55; *( data + ( p->len - 3 ) ) = 0x55; *( data + ( p->len - 4 ) ) = 0x55; } LWIP_MEMPOOL_FREE( RX_POOL, custom_pbuf ); ... // remaining function } 2. Send tcp packets to controller and back to pc in a loop. 3. Check if the packets sent and received are equal. 4. Soon (pretty much instant actually), this check will fail and the received packet will contain 32 bytes of 0x88 (sometimes including the 0x55 at the end). Screenshot of wireshark (log attached) [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Screenshot of a hex/ASCII memory dump viewer showing packet-like binary data. The left pane lists offsets from 0000 to 0130 with hexadecimal bytes; the right pane shows ASCII interpretation. The first bytes resemble an Ethernet/IPv4/TCP frame: destination MAC 34:48:ed:35:fc:82, source MAC 00:80:e1:00:00:08, EtherType 0x0800, followed by IP header bytes (starting with 45 01 ...), then TCP-like payload. The ASCII payload contains many printable random-looking substrings separated by non-printable bytes and repeated 0x88 filler-like bytes, consistent with a captured buffer or corrupted/unaligned network packet content. This image supports an issue about Ethernet RX / cache coherency because it looks like raw received frame data being inspected at buffer level. [IMAGE TEXT] 0000 34 48 ed 35 fc 82 00 80 e1 00 00 08 00 45 01 27 04 e6 00 00 ff 06 2e dc a8 02 fa c0 a8 02 c8 0b b8 f1 43 00 04 42 42 74 28 c5 60 50 18 14 c6 10 00 00 32 78 72 35 63 38 78 30 64 68 6f 7a 35 74 6b 71 6c 69 36 31 73 78 77 35 33 72 35 69 70 7b 31 73 37 6e 39 6f 72 65 79 2r 6d 7a 36 33 6c 67 6c 63 6e 67 51 37 33 32 72 6c 37 72 65 6c 67 33 31 6c 33 67 36 39 37 6f 65 7f 77 65 6c 67 39 33 34 39 36 69 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 88 6f 63 78 3h 72 72 65 73 6f 63 6a 69 32 73 66 78 74 6f 39 77 61 76 72 70 73 6c 73 67 70 35 69 38 33 6a 6f 71 61 66 61 69 31 6d 63 69 38 36 6a 31 37 67 70 61 63 7a 7r 32 34 6c 31 37 72 77 36 61 6d 6c 70 62 71 71 76 66 67 77 6s 1a 73 63 6f 74 30 68 66 76 0m 7a 31 68 35 68 63 6e 6d 67 36 66 69 71 72 61 62 72 37 30 68 6c 66 69 61 36 35 6f 75 7a 69 31 65 77 6b 79 7d 6e 6c 67 6a 69 66 35 30 6e 68 7a 31 6b 65 33 68 31 31 2a 67 6f 6e 61 69 61 31 70 37 6d 6b 62 73 31 67 64 6b 6a 6f 69 61 61 31 68 30 66 37 74 6c 39 74 30 68 66 76 6f 30 7d 7a 31 68 35 63 68 31 6c 62 61 39 6f 30 69 72 61 61 62 72 31 37 30 6c 3f 6d 65 6d 67 36 6f 65 61 66 31 70 31 72 62 72 31 31 66 65 36 65 61 63 7f 66 65 62 61 73 72 32 04 3c dc d6 **My solution** My solution add this to the function pbuf_free_custom, right before the line LWIP_MEMPOOL_FREE( RX_POOL, custom_pbuf );: void pbuf_free_custom( struct pbuf* p ) { ... // start of the function for( pbuf* q = p; q != nullptr; q = q->next ) { SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr( (uint32_t*) q->payload, q->len ); } LWIP_MEMPOOL_FREE( RX_POOL, custom_pbuf ); ... // remaining function } After adding these lines, the problem does not appear anymore. I will validate this solution further in the following days and then commit a PR when I am sure this fixes the bug. **Wireshark log** [st-cache-receive.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/10024097/st-cache-receive.zip)

Key comments:
I have done some further research, the combination of cache + DMA is known to be tricky. See this forum post: [Hint: DMA and cache coherency](https://community.st.com/s/question/0D50X00009XkhUWSAZ/hint-dma-and-cache-coherency) When the DMA writes data to the RxBuffers, it ignores the dcache. Any previously cached data is still valid, even after the pbuf memory is freed and overwritten by the DMA. So I am pretty confident that it is required to clear the dcache after freeing the pbuf memory, otherwise the memory written to by HAL_ETH_ReadData will contain invalid cache entries. A subsequent read of that memory location will read garbage bytes from the cache. ST Internal Reference: 158119 Hello @futurezeb, Thank you for your report. We partially reproduced your scenario: * 255-byte packets containing random data are sent by the PC. * The STM32 sends the packet back to the PC. * The PC compares the sent and received data and displays an error message if they are different. * The process is repeated if there is no error. However, we were unable to reproduce the issue. Please allow me to close this issue. You can reopen it at any time if you have any details to share with us.
