issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Bank mapping support is broken
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=150
Root cause: Hi @AAganichev, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** We use custom board with the external Flash connected to NOR/PSRAM Bank 1 **Describe the bug** There's two issues with the bank mapping support in SDK 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, usage_question, high, invalid, cube mx, projects, NOR, PSRAM, SDK, NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** We use custom board with the external Flash connected to NOR/PSRAM Bank 1 **Describe the bug** There's two issues with the bank mapping support in SDK 1.9.0: 1. NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS{1-4} are hardcoded in the stm32h7xx_hal_nor.h and not changed with the setting of bank mapping in CubeMX. 2. SDK 1.9.0 introduces access to the flash at the end of HAL_NOR_Init() which cause HardFault because of HAL_SetFMCMemorySwappingConfig() called after initializing of first bank. **How To Reproduce** 1. Set bank mapping in CubeMX to "NOR/PSRAM bank and SDRAM bank1/bank2 are swapped". 2. Setup "NOR Flash/PSRAM/SRAM/ROM/LCD 1" as NOR Flash 3. Correct NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS1 to point to 0xc0000000 in stm32h7xx_hal_nor.h 4. Write a test code to read data from 0xc0000000. 5. Run and get a HardFault inside HAL_NOR_Init(). **Additional context** I propose make definitions of NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS{1-4} dependent on swapping config.

Key comments:
Hi @AAganichev, Thank you for your contribution. In order to allow a better analysis of this problem, could you please give us more details about the application that you are using to reproduce this issue or did you use one of our applications? Otherwise, it is possible to share with us a code snippet allowing our development teams to reproduce it. Also, could you please confirm you are using the latest firmware version and that the issue is systematically reproducible on your side? Thank you again for your contribution. You don't need even specific application. You need a board with NOR Flash (though SRAM will also work for testing purpose) on CS1, configure CS as NOR Flash (even if it contains SRAM) and setup bank mapping. Then you have two options: 1) Add a single line to the generated from CubeMX application after memory init: volatile int i = *(volatile int *)NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS1; Run app and get HardFault because of NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS1 points to 0x60000000 instead of 0xc0000000. 2) Correct NOR_MEMORY_ADDRESS1 to point to 0xc0000000 in stm32h7xx_hal_nor.h as it should. Run application and you'll get HardFault because of access to memory before remapping. Hi @AAganichev,

issues.issue_title: STM32H7 RCC Driver Doesn't Support Changing HSIDIV When SYSCLK Using HSI
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: STM32H7 RCC Driver Doesn't Support Changing HSIDIV When SYSCLK Using HSI
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H7A3ZI, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=low, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=149
Root cause: Hi @paulr227, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: According to RM0455 it should be possible to change HSIDIV when HSI is selected as the system clock, as long as HSI is not used as the PLL Source and a PLL enabled: > Note that the HSIDIV cannot be changed if the HSI is selected as reference clock for at least one enabled PLL (PLLxON bit set to 1).
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7A3ZI, HAL, UART, configuration_help, low, cube mx, cube ide, RM0455, HSIDIV, HSI, PLL

Technical details:
According to RM0455 it should be possible to change HSIDIV when HSI is selected as the system clock, as long as HSI is not used as the PLL Source and a PLL enabled: > Note that the HSIDIV cannot be changed if the HSI is selected as reference clock for at least one enabled PLL (PLLxON bit set to 1). In that case the hardware does not update the HSIDIV with the new value. However it is possible to change the HSIDIV if the HSI is used directly as system clock. However, the condition on the following line evaluates to true and __HAL_RCC_HSE_CONFIG() is then never called to update HSIDIV. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_rcc.c#L482 E.g. if HSI_DIV4 is configured with CubeIDE's Clock Configuration (with PLLs off), CDCPRE=HPRE=DIV1, the following code is generated: void SystemClock_Config(void) { RCC_OscInitTypeDef RCC_OscInitStruct = {0}; RCC_ClkInitTypeDef RCC_ClkInitStruct = {0}; RCC_PeriphCLKInitTypeDef PeriphClkInitStruct = {0}; /** Supply configuration update enable */ HAL_PWREx_ConfigSupply(PWR_DIRECT_SMPS_SUPPLY); /** Configure the main internal regulator output voltage */ __HAL_PWR_VOLTAGESCALING_CONFIG(PWR_REGULATOR_VOLTAGE_SCALE0); while(!__HAL_PWR_GET_FLAG(PWR_FLAG_VOSRDY)) {} /** Initializes the RCC Oscillators according to the specified parameters * in the RCC_OscInitTypeDef structure. */ RCC_OscInitStruct.OscillatorType = RCC_OSCILLATORTYPE_HSI; RCC_OscInitStruct.HSIState = RCC_HSI_DIV4; RCC_OscInitStruct.HSICalibrationValue = RCC_HSICALIBRATION_DEFAULT; RCC_OscInitStruct.PLL.PLLState = RCC_PLL_NONE; if (HAL_RCC_OscConfig(&RCC_OscInitStruct) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } /** Initializes the CPU, AHB and APB buses clocks */ RCC_ClkInitStruct.ClockType = RCC_CLOCKTYPE_HCLK|RCC_CLOCKTYPE_SYSCLK |RCC_CLOCKTYPE_PCLK1|RCC_CLOCKTYPE_PCLK2 |RCC_CLOCKTYPE_D3PCLK1|RCC_CLOCKTYPE_D1PCLK1; RCC_ClkInitStruct.SYSCLKSource = RCC_SYSCLKSOURCE_HSI; RCC_ClkInitStruct.SYSCLKDivider = RCC_SYSCLK_DIV1; RCC_ClkInitStruct.AHBCLKDivider = RCC_HCLK_DIV1; RCC_ClkInitStruct.APB3CLKDivider = RCC_APB3_DIV2; RCC_ClkInitStruct.APB1CLKDivider = RCC_APB1_DIV2; RCC_ClkInitStruct.APB2CLKDivider = RCC_APB2_DIV2; RCC_ClkInitStruct.APB4CLKDivider = RCC_APB4_DIV2; if (HAL_RCC_ClockConfig(&RCC_ClkInitStruct, FLASH_LATENCY_0) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } PeriphClkInitStruct.PeriphClockSelection = RCC_PERIPHCLK_USART3; PeriphClkInitStruct.Usart234578ClockSelection = RCC_USART234578CLKSOURCE_HSI; if (HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig(&PeriphClkInitStruct) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } } The HSIDIV configuration will remain at DIV1, AXI clock at 64 MHz but the Flash LATENCY will be set to 0 wait states (max AXI clock for 0 WS, VOS0 is 42 MHz), resulting in an invalid configuration and the MCU entering an invalid state.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Wrong pin config in stm32h747i_eval_nor.c
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H747I, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=configuration_help, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=144
Root cause: My apology.
Fix: I reported this in #142 and #143, but they were closed without any effort from ST to discuss.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H747I, HAL, configuration_help, medium, GPIOC, gpio_init_structure, GPIO_AF9_FMC, GPIO_PIN_6, GPIO_PIN_7, HAL_GPIO_Init, GPIOD

Technical details:
I reported this in #142 and #143, but they were closed without any effort from ST to discuss. It's a nasty bug that took me a few days to figure out; so please fix it. This is in the current code: /* GPIOC configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF9_FMC; gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_6 | GPIO_PIN_7; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOC, &gpio_init_structure); /* GPIOD configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF12_FMC; //add GPIO_PIN_7 gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_0 | GPIO_PIN_1 | GPIO_PIN_4 | GPIO_PIN_5|GPIO_PIN_7|\ GPIO_PIN_8 | GPIO_PIN_9 | GPIO_PIN_10 | GPIO_PIN_11 |\ GPIO_PIN_12 | GPIO_PIN_13 | GPIO_PIN_14 | GPIO_PIN_15; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOD, &gpio_init_structure); What's wrong is PC6 and PC7 are not used for FMC in stm32h747i_eval (they're used for other purposes according to the board document), so they need to be removed here, and clock for GPIOC doesn't need to be turned on. Then GPIO_PIN_6 needs to be added to GPIOD init. So replace the above code with this: /* GPIOD configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF12_FMC; gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_0 | GPIO_PIN_1 | GPIO_PIN_4 | GPIO_PIN_5| GPIO_PIN_6| GPIO_PIN_7|\ GPIO_PIN_8 | GPIO_PIN_9 | GPIO_PIN_10 | GPIO_PIN_11 |\ GPIO_PIN_12 | GPIO_PIN_13 | GPIO_PIN_14 | GPIO_PIN_15; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOD, &gpio_init_structure);

Key comments:
My apology. You reopened #142. I'll close this now. Thanks for the fix.

Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H747I, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=142
Root cause: Hi @trinhnhatnam, Referring to the [datasheet](https://www.
Fix: This is in the current code: /* GPIOC configuration */ gpio_init_structure.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H747I, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, bsp, GPIOC, gpio_init_structure, GPIO_AF9_FMC, GPIO_PIN_6

Technical details:
This is in the current code: /* GPIOC configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF9_FMC; gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_6 | GPIO_PIN_7; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOC, &gpio_init_structure); /* GPIOD configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF12_FMC; //add GPIO_PIN_7 gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_0 | GPIO_PIN_1 | GPIO_PIN_4 | GPIO_PIN_5|GPIO_PIN_7|\ GPIO_PIN_8 | GPIO_PIN_9 | GPIO_PIN_10 | GPIO_PIN_11 |\ GPIO_PIN_12 | GPIO_PIN_13 | GPIO_PIN_14 | GPIO_PIN_15; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOD, &gpio_init_structure); What's wrong is PC6 and PC7 are not used for FMC, so they need to be removed, and clock for GPIOC doesn't need to be turned on. Then GPIO_PIN_6 needs to be added to GPIOD init. So replace the above code with this: /* GPIOD configuration */ gpio_init_structure.Alternate = GPIO_AF12_FMC; gpio_init_structure.Pin = GPIO_PIN_0 | GPIO_PIN_1 | GPIO_PIN_4 | GPIO_PIN_5| GPIO_PIN_6| GPIO_PIN_7|\ GPIO_PIN_8 | GPIO_PIN_9 | GPIO_PIN_10 | GPIO_PIN_11 |\ GPIO_PIN_12 | GPIO_PIN_13 | GPIO_PIN_14 | GPIO_PIN_15; HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOD, &gpio_init_structure);

Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H743ZI, HAL, ETH, medium, help wanted, projects, RTEMS, BSD, LwIP_HTTP_Server_Netconn_RTOS, SLA0044, legal_agreement

Technical details:
Hello, Thanks for providing the application examples for lwIP. They were very helpful for me as I am trying to port them to the RTEMS OS. However, there is still a small issue which makes it difficult to release the port as part of RTEMS which generally requires an OpenSource license like a BSD license. The example is licensed differently than the HAL library ( for example: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Netconn_RTOS) under the [ST Ultimate Liberty license SLA0044](https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/legal/legal_agreement/license_agreement/group0/87/0c/3d/ad/0a/ba/44/26/DM00216740/files/DM00216740.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.DM00216740.pdf) instead of the BSD 3-Clause. Point 5 of SLA0044 is especially problematic. My port is based on your example applications for lwIP (ethernetif.c, app_ethernet.c) , but was heavily modified to be usable for the RTEMS OS. Would it be possible to license these files under BSD 3-Clause, similarly to the HAL library? RTEMS would be willing to accept a BSD-style licence with vendor device restrictions in device driver/HAL code, but SLA0044 would be problematic. The LAN driver already seems to be licensed under BSD3 The project can be found here: https://github.com/rmspacefish/rtems-lwip/tree/0ef4b8a7d4d4d4ad9af90e36e4f9b2c457295ee5/lwip/ports/drivers/stm32h7 Thanks a lot in advance. Kind Regards Robin

I will try to push to have an answer as soon as possible. I will keep you informed. Thank you for your patience and comprehension and thank you again for having tackled the subject. Hi @rmspacefish, I hope you are fine. Your request is still under discussion. May I ask whether the ported code is intended to run on STMicroelectronics hardware exclusively once integrated into the RTEMS OS project? The ported code with the licensing issues glues the lwIP code to the STM32 and the used PHY so this part will be run on STMicroelectronics hardware exclusively. issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Query: Tweaking __main or updating / modifying SystemInit() to call System Clock Configure, Peripheral Configure and FMC Initialization before calling Zero Initialization of memory
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H753XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=low, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=134
Root cause: Hello, Please also help provide a user code section just before LDR R0, =__main in file startup_stm32h753xx.
Fix: Hello, I am currently unable to declare initialized Global Variables in External SRAM because of the limitations with __main function (available with Keil compiler version V6.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H753XX, HAL, usage_question, high, duplicate, enhancement, help wanted, good first issue, wontfix, cmsis, SRAM

Technical details:
Hello, I am currently unable to declare initialized Global Variables in External SRAM because of the limitations with __main function (available with Keil compiler version V6.16 ) code availability and use of STM32CubeMX (version 6.2.1). The generated code is using the HAL drivers for System Clock, Peripherals and FMC. I had earlier informed in one of my queries that when FMC is configured with STM32CubeMX, the tool does not embed details of the external SRAM to the SCT file that is used by Keil Compiler. I read the document [Application Startup](https://www.keil.com/support/man/docs/armclang_intro/armclang_intro_asa1505906246660.htm) and understand that if I want to declare an Initialized Global Variable in external FMC SRAM, then this can only be done by tweaking the __main or preceding __main execution with a function call / execution that: 1. Initializes Clocks 2. Initializes at least the the FMC Pins 3. Initializes the FMC communication (signal settings). On reviewing the function SystemInit, which is called before __main, I observe that the function only uses Microcontroller registers, and assigns constant values to the used registers, and I understand the reason for why variables are not used. Current understanding: 1. I understand that code of __main is available in some Keil provided library and hence cannot be tweaked. So the available option would be to call / execute a user function (which does some user required actions) before executing __main . 2. The STM32CubeMX provides function like SystemClock_Config(), PeriphCommonClock_Config() and MX_FMC_Init() which use at least some local variables / structures, and hence these functions cannot be called before calling __main. Considerations: 1. Not everyone who uses Keil and uses the SBM32 microcontrollers will be able to correctly tweak the the System Clock, Peripheral Configuration and FMC Initialization functions. 2. The STM32CubeMX tool will overwrite any tweaks that are made to above functions or any part of the code which are not present in the user section. Requests: 1. I would request you to please provide a custom (weak) function (called from within __main) that may be modified by user. This function call should exist: A. before the call that initializes global variables and zeroes the ZI section B. Exist after the stack is created. 2. If above is not possible, then help me with a tool that helps remove local variables and embed fix values in code, so that a user can create a Custom function from a stable function (generated by STM32CubeMX or provided by Keil) and executes the custom function before __main? 3. If even the above is not possible then please help me with a LL Driver for the three functions. the LL Driver must not use any variables and should be available / generated through the STM32CubeMX, when a future version of STM32CubeH7 is released. Please help me with your inputs. Thanks, @rxa1031

Key comments:
Hello, Please also help provide a user code section just before LDR R0, =__main in file startup_stm32h753xx.s. @rxa1031 Hello, When comparing the STM32CubeH7 / STM32CubeMX implementation with the Keil Provided CMSIS implementation, I found some inputs which I want to share with you. As per ARM / Keil, it is expected, all the memory used by the application is enabled before calling __main. In the CMSIS standard, the SystemInit() function is the place for this. I obviously macro DATA_IN_ExtSRAM and code for SRAM in System_st32f4xx.c file, which accompanies the STM32F4xx_DFP. void SystemInit(void) { /* FPU settings ------------------------------------------------------------*/ #if (__FPU_PRESENT == 1) && (__FPU_USED == 1) SCB->CPACR |= ((3UL << 10*2)|(3UL << 11*2)); /* set CP10 and CP11 Full Access */ #endif #if defined (DATA_IN_ExtSRAM) || defined (DATA_IN_ExtSDRAM) SystemInit_ExtMemCtl(); #endif /* DATA_IN_ExtSRAM || DATA_IN_ExtSDRAM */ /* Configure the Vector Table location add offset address ------------------*/ #ifdef VECT_TAB_SRAM SCB->VTOR = SRAM_BASE | VECT_TAB_OFFSET; /* Vector Table Relocation in Internal SRAM */ #else SCB->VTOR = FLASH_BASE |

Hello, Used tools and embedded software packs: STM32CubeMX version 6.2.1 STM32CubeH7 version 1.9.0 Keil compiler version V6.16 (Available with MDK534.EXE) Requirements: 1. Declare a Global variable with a known value in External SRAM: - NO-INIT / UNINIT section - INIT Section My understand is that the only difference between a NO-INIT / UNINIT and an INIT section is that the memory region marked with INIT is to be updated by function SystemInit such that all the bytes in that region are initialized with a value of 0. Where as the memory region declared as NO-INIT / UNINIT is not cleared. Peculiar issue: 1. Should the External SRAM details be also added to Options for Target'Project' -> Target -> Read/Write Memory Areas -> RAM1, RAM2 and RAM3? 4. issues.issue_title: Wrong HSE_VALUE in NUCLEO-H743ZI LwIP Application
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Wrong HSE_VALUE in NUCLEO-H743ZI LwIP Application
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H743ZI, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=132
Root cause: Hi @kkrambo, First we would like to thank you for your contribution.
Fix: The HSE_VALUE should be 0x08000000 instead of 0x25000000.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H743ZI, HAL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, projects, HSE_VALUE, HSE, MCO

Technical details:
The HSE_VALUE should be 0x08000000 instead of 0x25000000. (By default, the HSE is sourced from the fixed 8 MHz MCO from the ST-LINK microcontroller on the NUCLEO boards.) This bug might be benign for the lwIP application as it is. But it caused me grief when I updated the project to add a USART feature because it caused the baud rate to be incorrect. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Projects/NUCLEO-H743ZI/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Netconn_RTOS/Inc/stm32h7xx_hal_conf.h#L97

Key comments:
Hi @kkrambo, First we would like to thank you for your contribution. The issue you pointed out is confirmed. In fact, the HSE_VALUE value should be 8000000 instead of 25000000. An internal tracker has been logged and a fix will be implemented and made available in the frame of a future release. Thank you once again for your contribution. ST Internal Reference: 104729 Hi @kkrambo, This issue has been fixed in the frame of version v1.10.0 of the STM32CubeH7 published recently. Please allow me then to close this thread.

Problem: Query: USART RX FIFO
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=130
Root cause: Hi @rxa1031, The following are answers to the different questions raised within **"Inputs from my colleague"** section : 1.
Fix: Hello, I am using STM32CubeMX version 6.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, HAL, UART, usage_question, high, question, USART, FIFO, USART1, IRQ, TXE, TXFT

Technical details:
Hello, I am using STM32CubeMX version 6.2.0 and STM32CubeH7 version 1.9.0. I am concerned about the Asynchronous USART FIFO related settings, which I shall describe later in this discussion. **Pre-condition:** 1. Independent cyclic buffers exist for TX and RX data. 2. A Transmit task would write to the TX Buffer array (C variable), which will then be used in USART1 IRQ Handler to send out data. The Write task will only trigger TXE Interrupt (assuming FIFO not used) and let the IRQ Handler perform rest of the Functionality. (I am not sure whether to use TXFT or TXFE ISR bits in case of FIFO use enable) 3. A Task would check number of bytes available in RX Buffer array (C variable), and will use them if the number of available bytes are positive. 4. The USART1 IRQ handler code must always be ready to receive any byte that is sent to it. Code will _NOT call_ functions like the HAL_USART_Receive_IT() function to start receiving bytes. **Inputs from my colleague:** 1. Enable FIFO for both transmit and receive, with a 1/8 Depth threshold setting. _In fact, if the FIFO is not enabled, it can be difficult for the CPU to keep up with fast incoming data._ 2. Code does not have to depend on RX FIFO interrupts like the _RXFT_ and _RXFF_ but can rather use the _RXFNE_ interrupt for receiving bytes. **Concerns:** 1. I request your suggestion on my colleague's input. 2. I am assume my colleague's inputs are correct. However, if this is not the case, then while using the Asynchronous UART HAL or LL Driver, I am not sure how one could _ENABLE FIFO only for TX_, and _leave FIFO DISABLE for RX_ (to receive even a single byte) 3. If above is not possible then how to receive one byte using RX FIFO with USART_CR3_RXFTCFG = 0b000 and USART_CR3_RXFTIE = 1. 4. Is there a possibility to use IDLE, CTS and RTS to know when Reception started and when it ended? If so may you please help me understand more about this. **My understanding of RX FIFO:** 1. There are maximum of 16 RX FIFO available. 2. With USART_CR3_RXFTIE = 1, the smallest number of received bytes for which the interrupt will trigger is _2 bytes_. This can be set by setting USART_CR3_RXFTCFG = 0b000. Thus if only one byte is received, then this interrupt will not trigger. If I manually make changes to code and later regenerate code using the STM32CubeMX tool any changes made to (non user related) STM32CubeMX generated code parts will get overwritten. Please help. Thanks, Rajeev

Key comments:
Hi @rxa1031, The following are answers to the different questions raised within **"Inputs from my colleague"** section : 1. The FIFO feature is indeed useful for fast data transfer and it allows the CPU to keep up with fast incoming data. 2. The user code may depend on both RXFT and RXFF interrupts as well as RXFNE. However, only RXFNE is managed within the HAL_UART_IRQHandler(). For the rest it's up to the user to handle them and define his own interruption routines to execute when RXFT or RXFF interrupts are set. The following are answers to the different questions raised within **"Concerns"** section : 1. Answered in the section above. 2. Enabling the FIFO feature will automatically enable the transmit FIFO (TXFIFO) and the receive FIFO (RXFIFO). It is not possible to activate only one of them. However, you have the ability to enable or disable the interruptions related to the transmit FIFO or receive FIFO thru **USART_CR1_RXFFIE** and **USART_CR1_TXFEIE** bits. It is also possible to handle separately the transmit and receive FIFO threshold configurations as well as enabling or disabling the RXFIFO and TXFIF threshold interrupt separately using **USART_CR3_RXFTIE** an

Hello, browsing through the timer header I spotted that the description of the one pulse mode is swapped for single and repetive mode. /** @defgroup TIM_LL_EC_ONEPULSEMODE One Pulse Mode * @{ */ #define LL_TIM_ONEPULSEMODE_SINGLE TIM_CR1_OPM /*!< Counter is not stopped at update event */ #define LL_TIM_ONEPULSEMODE_REPETITIVE 0x00000000U /*!< Counter stops counting at the next update event */ /** * @} */ I think this should be: /** @defgroup TIM_LL_EC_ONEPULSEMODE One Pulse Mode * @{ */ #define LL_TIM_ONEPULSEMODE_SINGLE TIM_CR1_OPM /*!< Counter stops counting at the next update event */ #define LL_TIM_ONEPULSEMODE_REPETITIVE 0x00000000U /*!< Counter is not stopped at update event */ /** * @} */ Hope this helps. Fix: Hello, In the datasheet I observe below information when checking bits available with **USART_CR2**: _Bit 23 **RTOEN**: Receiver timeout enable This bit is set and cleared by software.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, UART, usage_question, medium, question, USART_CR2, RTOEN, RTOF, USART_ISR, RTOR

Technical details:
Hello, In the datasheet I observe below information when checking bits available with **USART_CR2**: _Bit 23 **RTOEN**: Receiver timeout enable This bit is set and cleared by software. 0: Receiver timeout feature disabled. 1: Receiver timeout feature enabled. When this feature is enabled, the RTOF flag in the USART_ISR register is set if the RX line is idle (no reception) for the duration programmed in the RTOR (receiver timeout register)._ I however do not observe the check added to below code in the ISR service routine: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L2294 Please suggest whether the code must be modified. Thanks, Rajeev

Key comments:
Assuming I am using the LL Driver, should the updated check be: if( LL_USART_IsEnabledRxTimeout(phLocalUART) && LL_USART_IsEnabledIT_RTO(phLocalUART) && READ_BIT( phLocalUART->ISR, LL_USART_ISR_RTOF ) == LL_USART_ISR_RTOF ) { WRITE_REG(phLocalUART->ICR, USART_ICR_RTOCF); } Hi @rxa1031, Referring to the HAL driver, the **USART_CR1_RTOIE** bit could be enabled within the [HAL_UART_Receive_DMA()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L1489) and [HAL_UART_Receive_IT()](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L1370) APIs after checking on the **USART_CR2_RTOEN** state as follows : https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/ccb11556044540590ca6e45056e6b65cdca2deb2/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_uart.c#L1506-L1512 The USART_CR1_RTOIE state is closely dependent on the state of USART_CR2_RTOEN bit. Thus, receiver timeout interrupt can only be enabled if **USART_CR2_RTOEN** is already set. Hence, if the receiver timeout feature is enabled.

Technical details:
CubeMX generated code does not align MDMA linked list nodes to double word addresses as required. This prevents MDMA from functioning when using linked list mode. [IMAGE DESCRIPTION] Screenshot of an STM32 reference manual page for the MDMA controller, section 14.5.11 “MDMA channel x link address register (MDMA_CxLAR)”. It shows the register bitfield layout for LAR[31:0] with the lower 3 bits highlighted by the rule text below stating the link address must be Double Word aligned. 14.5.11 MDMA channel x link address register (MDMA_CxLAR)
In Linked List mode, at the end of a block (single or last block in repeated block transfer mode), this register is loaded from memory (from address given by current LAR[31:0] + 0x14).

Note: The new value is only taken into account after all registers are updated, for the next end of block.

Address offset: 0x64 + 0x40 × x, (x = 0 to 15)
Reset value: 0x0000 0000

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Ethernet: write to SYSCFG before MAC reset require wait
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H743ZI, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=121
Root cause: Hi @amurzeau, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-H743ZI * IDE: STM32CubeIDE v1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H743ZI, HAL, ETH, usage_question, high, mw, IDE, HPRE, APB4, MAC, STM32

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Board: NUCLEO-H743ZI * IDE: STM32CubeIDE v1.5.1 * STM32CubeH7 Firmware v1.8.0 **Describe the bug** When using a system clock of 400 Mhz, a HPRE prescaler of /2 and a APB4 divisor of /16, the ethernet MAC does not initialize correctly. In that case, ethernet does not work (no ping from a PC) **How To Reproduce** 1. Generate a project using LwIP 2. Configure a /16 APB4 prescaler and a /2 HPRE prescaler 3. Run the project and try to ping the STM32 from a PC 4. The ping fails 5. Change the APB4 prescaler to something like /2 and reflash the board 6. The ping works 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...) In [stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c in function HAL_ETH_Init](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.c#L327), when adding (void)SYSCFG->PMCR like this, the ethernet MAC is correctly initialized. c if(heth->Init.MediaInterface == HAL_ETH_MII_MODE) { HAL_SYSCFG_ETHInterfaceSelect(SYSCFG_ETH_MII); } else { HAL_SYSCFG_ETHInterfaceSelect(SYSCFG_ETH_RMII); } (void)SYSCFG->PMCR; // Adding this line will fix the issue and make ethernet works again /* Ethernet Software reset */ /* Set the SWR bit: resets all MAC subsystem internal registers and logic */ /* After reset all the registers holds their respective reset values */ SET_BIT(heth->Instance->DMAMR, ETH_DMAMR_SWR); The reason is probably that: * SYSCFG peripheral uses the APB4 peripheral clock * When setting the RMII/MII configuration, it takes more clock pulses to be taken into account because of the /16 APB4 prescaler (and maybe also /2 HPRE prescaler) * When executing the Ethernet Software reset, the SYSCFG RMII/MII muxes might not be configured yet * As state in the datasheet for the DMAMR register, bit SWR, doing the ethernet software reset requires to have all PHY input clocks established: > The reset operation is complete only when all resets in all active clock domains are deasserted. Therefore, it is essential that all PHY inputs clocks (applicable for the selected PHY interface) are present for software reset completion. The time to complete the software reset operation depends on the frequency of the slowest active clock. So to ensure all PHY inputs clocks are present, the RX and TX clocks must be correctly muxed via the SYSCFG block. This requires to add a dummy read or a delay to ensure the write to SYSCFG->PMCR[EPIS] is taken into account before doing the ethernet software reset.

Dear @RKOUSTM I checked your response for #68 and #31 Used STM32CubeMX version 6.2.0 with STM32CubeMX along with latest released STM32CubeH7 package version **1.9.0** **I still observe an issue for a particular scenario.** **Good Behavior / Scenario** At least one byte must have been received via the Asynchronous UART port after a call to HAL_UART_Receive_IT() API is made. In this scenario the _Receiver Timeout interrupt triggers_ after the specified time, **BAD Behavior / Scenario** If _NOT EVEN A SINGLE BYTE_ is received over Asynchronous UART after the HAL_UART_Receive_IT() API is executed, then the Receiver Timeout (RTOF) interrupt present with the UART related USART_ISR **NEVER SETS** and hence the _interrupt never triggers_ even though the related bits in USART_CR1 and USART_CR2 are set. Please help me understand how to fix above issue. With help of Receiver Timeout interrupt I want to ensure that: 1. The connected device started to communicate within a defined time period. 2. The response was not sent by connected device and hence data need to be retransmitted 3. Possibly loose connection or cable break Please suggest what changes need to be made. Thanks, Rajeev

Key comments:
Sample code attached for reference: [Gateway-H7-App-with-STM32CubeH7-ver-1.9.0-from-scratch-20210309-2311-IST.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/6110532/Gateway-H7-App-with-STM32CubeH7-ver-1.9.0-from-scratch-20210309-2311-IST.zip) Hi @rxa1031, The Receiver Timeout event is triggered when line has been in idle state for a programmable time. Receiver timeout is expressed in terms of bit duration and it is applicable only once the transfer occurred. In fact, the receiver timeout counter starts counting from the received stop bit, in other words, as soon as a character is received. As described in the [reference manual ](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/dm00314099-stm32h742-stm32h743-753-and-stm32h750-value-line-advanced-arm-based-32-bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) in the **"USART receiver timeout register (USART_RTOR)"** section : > In standard mode, the RTOF flag is set if, after the last received character, no new start bit is detected for more than the RTO value. This is explained in more details within the **"USART receiver timeout"** section : > The receiver timeout counter starts counting: > • from the end of the stop bit if STO

Problem: SPI and DMA is broken (no completion callback and stuck BUSY)
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H723, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=115
Root cause: Hi @tringis, First we would like to thank you for your contribution.
Fix: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA is broken for H7 because the callback SPI_DMATransmitCplt() in stm32h7xx_hal_spi.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H723, HAL, DMA, usage_question, high, invalid, projects, HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA, SPI_DMATransmitCplt, DMA_CIRCULAR, HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback

Technical details:
HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA is broken for H7 because the callback SPI_DMATransmitCplt() in stm32h7xx_hal_spi.c doesn't really do anything unless Mode is DMA_CIRCULAR. Specifically, it doesn't call the completion callback HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback() and it also doesn't set the State to HAL_SPI_STATE_READY (which causes the next call to HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA to fail). The functions HAL_SPI_Receive_DMA() and HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_DMA() have the same problem. **How To Reproduce** 1. Compile test program "SPI_FullDuplex_ComDMA" for NUCLEO-H723. 2. Set a breakpoint on HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback 3. Run the program 4. The breakpoint is never reached

Key comments:
Hi @tringis, First we would like to thank you for your contribution. We have checked the example **SPI_FullDuplex_ComDMA** for NUCLEO-H723 and it is working correctly. The example did access the HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback where LED1 and LED2 are activated to notify that transfer is completed. Please make sure you are correctly connecting the Master and Slave boards as mentioned in the [readme](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Projects/NUCLEO-H723ZG/Examples/SPI/SPI_FullDuplex_ComDMA/readme.txt). Root cause: Hi @basvloon, First we would like to thank you for pointing this out.
Fix: Hello, after debugging my timer interface I have found the following macros are missing a check for TIM12: - IS_TIM_MASTER_INSTANCE(), TIM12 allows master mode setting (MMS) although it only allows to drive a DMA 'channel'.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XXXX, DMA, bug_report, medium, enhancement, spotted before customer, internal bug tracker, cmsis, TIM12, IS_TIM_MASTER_INSTANCE, MMS

Technical details:
Hello, after debugging my timer interface I have found the following macros are missing a check for TIM12: - IS_TIM_MASTER_INSTANCE(), TIM12 allows master mode setting (MMS) although it only allows to drive a DMA 'channel'. - IS_TIM_CLOCKSOURCE_ITRX_INSTANCE(), TIM12 allows setting an internal input trigger. - IS_TIM_CLOCKSOURCE_TIX_INSTANCE(), TIM12 supports external clock mode 1. Maybe there are more issues regarding TIM12 but did not check further. I can also confirm issue reported at [https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/91](url). Potential patch to fix TIM12 checks: --- STM32H7xxxx.orig/CMSIS_HAL/Device/ST/STM32H7xx/Include/stm32h750xx.h 2021-02-14 12:48:21.997908200 +0800 +++ STM32H7xxxx/CMSIS_HAL/Device/ST/STM32H7xx/Include/stm32h750xx.h 2021-02-14 13:08:38.862692100 +0800 @@ -26124,6 +26124,7 @@ ((INSTANCE) == TIM6) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM7) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM8) || \ + ((INSTANCE) == TIM12) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM15)) /****** TIM Instances : Salve mode available (TIMx_SMCR.TS available )*********/ @@ -26300,6 +26301,7 @@ ((INSTANCE) == TIM4) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM5) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM8) || \ + ((INSTANCE) == TIM12) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM15) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM16) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM17)) @@ -26330,6 +26332,7 @@ ((INSTANCE) == TIM4) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM5) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM8) || \ + ((INSTANCE) == TIM12) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM15)) /****************** TIM Instances : supporting internal trigger inputs(ITRX) *******/ @@ -26340,6 +26343,7 @@ ((INSTANCE) == TIM4) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM5) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM8) || \ + ((INSTANCE) == TIM12) || \ ((INSTANCE) == TIM15)) /****************** TIM Instances : supporting OCxREF clear *******************/ Hope this helps. Best Regards, Bas

Key comments:
Hi @basvloon, First we would like to thank you for pointing this out. Regarding the first macro IS_TIM_MASTER_INSTANCE(), the issue has already been dealt and fixed internally. The fix will be part of the next release. For the remaining macros, IS_TIM_CLOCKSOURCE_ITRX_INSTANCE() and IS_TIM_CLOCKSOURCE_TIX_INSTANCE(), you're absolutely right, TIM12 is missing and should be added. This fix will be made available in the frame of a next release as well as the fix of the issue #91 which has been also confirmed . Thank you once again for your contribution and hope to hear from you again. ST Internal Reference: 101417 ST Internal Reference: 98873 Related to #91. Hi @basvloon, I hope you are fine. The issue you reported has been fixed in the frame of version **v1.9.1** of the STM32CubeH7 published recently on GitHub. Thank you again for having reported.

issues.issue_title: STM32CubeIDE Default Code for Nucleo H743ZI Includes Ethernet Bug
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: STM32CubeIDE Default Code for Nucleo H743ZI Includes Ethernet Bug
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=ETH, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=low, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=113
Root cause: Hi @RJ-400, Thank you for this post.
Fix: CubeMX provides a default Ethernet configuration for Nucleo boards incorporating an unassigned NULL pointer to which the MAC address is written.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, HAL, ETH, usage_question, low, cube mx, NULL, MAC, ITCM, STM32H7, AMAZING, ENORMOUS

Technical details:
CubeMX provides a default Ethernet configuration for Nucleo boards incorporating an unassigned NULL pointer to which the MAC address is written. When written, this corrupts the zero wait state, deterministic tightly coupled instruction memory (ITCM) located at 0x00000000 such that anyone locating code there will face a particularly nasty bug, just when they're making the already challenging leap, attempting to load code to and run code from ITCM, which in principle doesn't need to be so hard. The STM32H7 series hardware is AMAZING. The STM32CubeIDE and the low cost Nucleo boards are invaluable. But it's a long road to getting H7 devices to deliver the performance they're capable of, like 550 Mflops from a sub $3 H730VB device, for example! Rather than wasting nearly all that immense computational power faster than the hardware guys can serve it up, software guys should count clock cycles, look at the often ENORMOUS gaps between what they're getting and what the hardware was brilliantly engineered to achieve, and close the gaps... completely. It takes much more than clock configuration. To get there, you need: - Both ICache and Dcache, understanding their impact on zero wait state performance and single cycle instruction execution as well as the overhead, risks and complications involved in keeping the regular RAM in sync with the cache. - Both ITCM and DTCM (tightly coupled memory), understanding their more deterministic impact on zero wait state performance and single cycle execution - The ability to use linker scripts and startup assembly code to configure memory in a way that locates code, initialized data and uninitialized data in TCM. (AFIK, Cube doesn't help with this.) - The ability to load code and data from ultra cheap 2MB-256MB external serial flash into internal SRAM, especially zero wait state tightly coupled internal SRAM. (Executing at zero wait states from flash is nice, and ST's approaches to getting zero wait state performance from flash are superb, but if you have a lot of code and you put it all in internal flash, the cost per MB for that flash will be high.) - The ability to move code AT RUNTIME into the RAM section of choice. - A little bit of tight assembly language for DSP (DSP coding with VMUL.F32 and VADD.F32 is even easier than coding in C. Make good use of all 32 single precision floating point registers. Make good use of the 64 bit AXI bus. Make good use of the ability to execute loads and stores to and from TCM memory IN PARALLEL with most (but not MAC type) floating point calculations, all in a single clock cycle! - A little bit of tight assembly for moving data. - A clear understanding of how to get single cycle execution of floating point instructions. It appears that on the STM32F7 and H7, due to the nature of the pipeline that enables their incredible performance, you can't use the result of a floating point operation until THE THIRD clock cycle after the result is calculated. This is a pretty serious constraint, but you can still get great results under many circumstances if you write your code around it, but you have to know about it first, and it's a major science project to figure out all this vital (but undocumented?) stuff. Similarly, the cortex M7 floating point MAC instructions such as vfma.f32 and vmla.f32 CAN deliver single cycle performance, but not when loading/storing in parallel, and apparently, only when executing a sequence of instructions consisting only of MAC instructions. Why aren't these characteristics in Arm's Cortex M7 Technical Reference Manual?? At least some of these characteristics ARE addressed for the M4 in the Cortex M4 Technical Reference Manual. Are these factors for the M7 based devices addressed anywhere in ST documentation? Shouldn't this information be in the programming manuals? The datasheet? The reference manual? If not, where should it be? - The ability to write assembly code in a separate file, rather than using inline assembly, avoiding all that inline messiness and chaos. - The use of underscore underscore " __attribute__((section (".TCM_Code"), aligned(4))) " or similar specifiers before C function definitions and variable declarations to put code and data where you want it in RAM. Similarly, the use of " .section .TCM_Code.MyASMFunction " above assembly code routines in .s assembly files to designate where in memory they should be located. External assembly functions that are part of a project may be called from C after declaring them with " extern uint32_t MyASMFunction(uint32_t n, float* pbuf, float a, float b, float c, float d) asm ("MyASMFunction"); ". - Knowledge of the simple Arm EABI procedure call standards to efficiently call assembly code from C without wasted call overhead. - DMA! MDMA! It's not a hassle. It's a sublime luxury, and the H7 is DMA nirvana. Cube is great for setting it up, but you need to be looking at the programming manual while you do it, at least the first couple of times. - A cheap Saleae Logic probe for many reasons, including for counting cycles, because the numbers you get from the DWT cycle counter are often inaccurate. (If it's not fundamentally impossible due to the pipeline, we need a cycle counter that provides an accurate count in CubeIDE. Is this an Arm (Cortex) problem, an STM32 problem or a CubeIDE problem?) Much of this approach to performance is contrary to prevailing mindsets. Here's why the majority is wrong. Most computationally intensive code doesn't come close to achieving a floating point operation per clock cycle. It might be more like 20 clock cycles per floating point operation when all the application overhead is accounted for. Writing assembly language to save a clock cycle per flop under such circumstances only speeds things up by about 5%, and most think it's not worth it. But if you put in the effort to get it down to just two cycles per flop, the effort put into the last wasted clock cycle takes you from 275 Mflops to 550, effectively doubling the computational power of your design. Unlike many things, in this case, the closer you get to perfect, the GREATER the rewards for improvements. This isn't governed by the law of diminishing returns. Clock cycles are in the denominator. This is governed by the law of exploding returns. If you recognize that the difference between a 200MHz device and a 400MHz device matters, you have to recognize that doubling performance "for free" by eliminating the last wasted clock cycle also matters. But when you're starting out with one of these remarkable STM32 chips on a Nucleo board using MX and the CubeIDE, you're not really pointed in the right direction on the path to getting there, for a number of reasons, and I think they're rooted in the fact that the people developing CubeMX, the IDE, the low level drivers, the HAL and the examples aren't ever trying to make the devices do what they're capable of. If they were, the system and process would unfold differently. It's easy to blame it all on a bloated and buggy HAL that's nonetheless necessary and priceless as a means to timely basic functional success with a device that has 3000+ pages of documentation. Cube provides a starting point from which a streamlined design may be developed. But the knowledge necessary to make the H7, for example, go fast, doesn't unfold from the MX and Cube approach. Mflops should be the top priority in some of the examples, especially for devices like the H7. The "Blinky"s and "Hello world!"s should become "here's how we sum 64k floating point numbers in RAM in as close to one flop per max clock speed clock cycle". Some should use the I and D caches. Some should use TCM. Some should use MDMA. As fast as possible should be the default in many of the examples. What we have now is a bunch of newbies not getting past something akin to 16 MHz blinky with 7 wait states on ultra high performance hardware... (Okay, I'm exaggerating a bit). Even the experts are saying you don't need assembly language, and in the rare instances that you do, inline assembly is all you'll ever need. This is wrong. A platform like the STM32H7 is made for the performance that comes with zero wait states and tight assembly. In their development platforms, it's as if ST is using a Bugatti to pull a wagon on a hay ride. You get your fourth new Nucleo board weeks after the first Nucleo H7's become available, kind of set it up to go fast in CubeIDE, leaving the default devices on the board enabled, like Ethernet, for example, because you might need it soon, then you start to learn. When you eventually figure out that you should make use of TCM and put code there, starting at 0x00000000 or course, everything comes crashing down, and you think it's because you really might not be smart enough to write code for an STM32H7. Then you'll probably give up. But if you don't, eventually you'll figure out that in its init function, the Ethernet implementation provided by MX is writing the MAC address to an unassigned NULL pointer aimed right at the code you're trying to run in ITCM. You'll have to look at a memory dump to see what's going on. It was a bad default configuration generated by CubeMX, one that guarantees that pretty much everyone trying to make the fast microcontroller on their Nucleo board go fast in a deterministic way will fail. But that's the most important and valuable characteristic of the H7! Not good for sales. Yet years go by and nobody seems to care enough to figure it out, let alone fix it. But they knew there was a problem. That's why they put a warning in MX. Perhaps Nucleo boards and CubeIDE really were just for sales engineers who needed a snazzy way to run blinky. No. They're too valuable. But how could you let this go so long? It must be that virtually no one is making these boards go fast, whether they're customers or ST engineers. If they were, bugs like this would have been uncovered before the board was released, or worst case, shortly afterward, and getting performance from these devices wouldn't require weeks or months of detective work and reverse engineering to understand what ST should have conveyed in a 20 page document. This is a huge waste. Your hardware engineers should be fuming. Your software engineers should be dissatisfied. Your marketing people should be livid, at least the ones who aren't *#@($)! enough to think that crippling high performance platforms enables upselling. There's a big problem with tech education in America. The gap between textbook knowledge and its application is way too large. People should be able to take a couple of DSP courses and, at home or as part of a lab, sit down with a Nucleo board and run their filters and algorithms at the speed that modern, cost effective hardware is capable of. The mindset should not be "Start with low performance on high performance hardware, because, for those getting started, high performance doesn't matter. We'll save that for the elite experts who have the decades of experience to navigate our elite sophisticated product." The mindset should be "Start with high performance on high performance hardware, because that's what were selling, that's what the customer is buying, and for those getting started (and everyone else), high performance does matter, especially to those who don't want to get left in the dust." Extend the Cube philosophy by adding UI functionality for configuring devices appropriately and optimally for DSP, use of TCM, code location, assembly language, maximum floating point operations per second, etc. If you did that, some of the ST software bugs that cripple new users of your hardware would never occur. Maybe you could add a performance tab page to Cube. On it, you could configure code location, runtime relocation with function pointers, assembly language stubs, C to assembly interfacing, alignment, linker script generation, startup file generation and whatever else is necessary to get as close as possible to one floating point operation per clock cycle out of both TCM and cache, and provide instruction timing characteristics, constraints and code examples. Another tab page could be added for DSP, setting up biquads, basic IIR and FIR filters and matrix operations using C, assembly and CMSIS approaches. Hope you can get the Ethernet bug fixed.

Regarding the other points you mentioned, a list will be forwarded to our technical committee to study the possibility to integrate such enhancements into our software offer. Technical details:
Hello, According to the 'slave' functionality of the USART IP you can set the clock phase and polarity, which I would expect. In LL_USART_ClockInit there is no implementation to set the clock phase and polarity in case CLK_EN is off, which is should be done and is valid valid in case the IP is used in slave mode. At least according to the RM. Quote from RM: When the peripheral is used in SPI slave mode, the frequency of peripheral clock source (usart_ker_ck_pres) must be greater than 3 times the CK input frequency. The CPOL bit and the CPHA bit in the USART_CR2 register are used to select the clock polarity and the phase of the external clock, respectively (see Figure 583). An underrun error flag is available in slave transmission mode. This flag is set when the first clock pulse for data transmission appears while the software has not yet loaded any value to USART_TDR. The slave supports the hardware and software NSS management. Am I wrong or is this not correctly implemented ? Thanks for the feedback. Best Regards, Bas

Indeed, the actual implementation of the LL_USART_ClockInit() is incorrect and won't allow the clock phase and the clock polarity configuration when CR2_CLKEN is cleared. A fix will be implemented and will made available in the frame of a next release. ST Internal Reference: 98043 Hi @basvloon, I hope you are fine. Hello, Microcontroller in use: STM32H753BIT6 My code uses: HAL_NVIC_SetPriority(USART1_IRQn, 5, 0); HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ(USART1_IRQn); Macro configASSERT is defined. My code calls xQueueReceiveFromISR() inside the USART1_IRQ. I am observing issue with xQueueReceiveFromISR() (which is called with help of osMessageQueueGet()) When I analyzed the issue it turned out that ASSERT was triggered at https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/GCC/ARM_CM4F/port.c#L754 inside function vPortValidateInterruptPriority(). I had to change lines: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/GCC/ARM_CM4F/port.c#L72-L73 to: #define portFIRST_USER_INTERRUPT_NUMBER ( 6 ) #define portNVIC_IP_REGISTERS_OFFSET_16 ( 0xE000E3FA ) Also, I had to change line: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/GCC/ARM_CM4F/port.c#L729 to: ucCurrentPriority = *(pcInterruptPriorityRegisters + ulCurrentInterrupt); To fix the ASSERT issue. Please let me know your inputs. Thanks, @rxa1031

Key comments:
ulCurrentInterrupt = 0x25 Errata: Code was using TIM2 IRQ and not UART1 IRQ The actual problem is not the portNVIC_IP_REGISTERS_OFFSET_16 or portFIRST_USER_INTERRUPT_NUMBER values. The issue exists because of #define TICK_INT_PRIORITY ((uint32_t)0U) /*!< tick interrupt priority */ And its use during configuring the Timer that is used by FreeRTOS. _If xQueueReceiveFromISR() is called inside the FreeRTOS Timer interrupt the value copied to ucCurrentPriority (inside function vPortValidateInterruptPriority()) is ZERO._ I am collecting some more details with regards to _HAL_InitTick() which seems to be the culprit for FreeRTOS timer's priority setting_ and also might help me elaborate on #71 observations. @rxa1031 Hello @ASELSTM , I observe concerns with FreeRTOS file GCC\ARM_CM4\port.c. I am observing two ASSERTS / concerns in the file (triggered as a result of Reading from or Writing to a Queue from ISR): **First Issue:** Is observed for configASSERT( ucCurrentPriority >= ucMaxSysCallPriority ); when variable uwTickPrio = TICK_INT_PRIORITY (either assigned directly or with help of variable TickPriority), where macro TICK_INT_PRIORITY is assigned a value of 0.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: incorrect implementation of pvPortMalloc by the heap_4.c of FreeRTOS
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7B3I, component=FREERTOS, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=85
Root cause: Hi @TheSilentDawn, Thank you for this report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Development board: STM32H7B3I-DK and STM32H7B3I-EVAL * IDE and version: STMCubeIDE 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3I, Middleware, FREERTOS, usage_question, medium, wontfix, mw, third party, rtos, STM32H7B3I-DK, STM32H7B3I-EVAL

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Development board: STM32H7B3I-DK and STM32H7B3I-EVAL * IDE and version: STMCubeIDE 1.4.0 **Describe the bug** The function pvPortMalloc() is used to allocate memory for the required size. The parameter xWantedSize indicates the length of memory required. However, when the required memory block size is zero. The memory pointer variable pvReturn will keep as NULL. If the configuration configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK is enabled, it will recognize the variable xWantedSize valued zero as an error and handle it with the function vApplicationMallocFailedHook() as shown in https://github.com/FreeRTOS/FreeRTOS-Kernel/blob/5fb26de0194b4ebfd09b37128bf9f3ff6d34c1b7/portable/MemMang/heap_4.c#L253 (also https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/MemMang/heap_4.c#L249) **How To Reproduce** 1. Import the Domenstration example ClockAndWeather of the board STM32H7B3I-DK. 2. Enable macro configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK. This is default enabled when I try to debug the program. 3. Run the firmware with a default configuration to reproduce and it will loop infinitely. 4. This problem is caused by the incorrect implementation of the function pvPortMalloc() by heap_4.c of FreeRTOS. This bug is already reported to FreeRTOS as shown in https://github.com/FreeRTOS/FreeRTOS-Kernel/issues/204. **Additional context** To patch it, should return NULL or the next available heap address when the parameter xWantedSize is zero.

Key comments:
Hi @TheSilentDawn, Thank you for this report. Unfortunately, for this point, we don't treat aspect related to FreeRTOS in our GitHub repositories. As the heap_4.c file is out of the scope of STMicroelectronics, any modifications concerning this file are not implemented by our technical team. Please allow me to close this issue now. Thank you for your contribution.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3, Middleware, USB, bug_report, medium, enhancement, internal bug tracker, mw, MCU, MPU, USBH_ParseCfgDesc

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** - Software: - STM32Cube MCU & MPU Packages - Version: - STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.8.0 - Verification Hardware Platform: - STM32H7B3 **Describe the bug** - Function: - static void USBH_ParseCfgDesc(USBH_CfgDescTypeDef *cfg_desc, uint8_t *buf, uint16_t length) - Location: - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L420 - Type: - Buffer Overflow. - Result: - The system will parse the wrong descriptor. - Description: - The function USBH_ParseCfgDesc() parses the configuration descriptor, interface descriptor, and endpoint descriptor by input data from a USB device. - It tries to parse the endpoint descriptor when the variable pdesc->bDescriptorType is equal to USB_DESC_TYPE_ENDPOINT as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L420. If the variable pdesc->bDescriptorType is not equal to USB_DESC_TYPE_ENDPOINT, the firmware will try to access further memory until reaching the number pif->bNumEndpoints as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L417. If the variable cfg_desc->wTotalLength is also malformed, the firmware will overflow. In case the *host* has a reference to base itself on, then would it not also make sense to check the validity of this reference too? I hope my questions make sense. My goal is to be sure I understood correctly your point before reporting it to our development teams. I am looking forward to reading your reply. Thank you again. Hi @ALABSTM, No, I think the software embedded within the host should check if the hardware or the board supports or enables the wake-up feature. If not, the firmware shouldn't check bmAttributes as the current logic which will lead the whole system to hang. And to patch it, the wake-up feature checking codes should be added before the bmAttributes is accessed in the function and position reported upper. If anything not clear, please let me know. Root cause: Hi @TheSilentDawn, Thank you for your interest in our products and software solutions.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7B3, Middleware, USB, bug_report, high, enhancement, internal bug tracker, mw, MCU, MPU, USBH_ParseDevDesc

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** - Software: - STM32Cube MCU & MPU Packages - Version: - STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.8.0 - Verification Hardware Platform: - STM32H7B3 **Describe the bug** - Function: - static void USBH_ParseDevDesc(USBH_DevDescTypeDef *dev_desc, uint8_t *buf, uint16_t length) - Location: - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L355 - Type: - Denial-of-Service. - Result: - A malformed USB device packet may cause the system to hang when it tries to communicate with the outside world. - Description: - The function USBH_ParseDevDesc() parses the device descriptor by input data from a USB device. - The valid max packet size of the device descriptor should be 8, 16, 32, and 64 as USB specification required. However, the function USBH_ParseDevDesc() doesn’t check the value of dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L355. The variable dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize will be used as the size to construct the control pipe between host and device as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_core.c#L828. If bMaxPacketSize is zero, the firmware will get the error status USBH_FAIL in the function USBH_HandleControl() called by the function USBH_CtlReq() when trying to communicate with the outside world by IN and OUT pipe in the future and the host will try to re-enumerate. This process will loop again and again. **How To Reproduce** 1. Running MSC_Standalone application on the STM32H7B3I platform 2. Plug a USB disk 3. Use the attached Bug1.txt to replace the USB device packet. [Bug1.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/5381197/Bug1.txt) **Additional context** - To patch it, the program should check if dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize is equal to 8, 16, 32 or 64. At least, it should be greater than zero.

Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, HAL, FREERTOS, usage_question, high, question, cube mx, RKOUSTM, MCU, STM32H7, CMSIS

Technical details:
Hello @RKOUSTM , After a generated code with help of STM32CubeMX (with STM32Cube MCU Package for STM32H7 Series version 1.8.0), which has FreeRTOS enabled and uses CMSIS V2, I _added endless while loops_ to both the assert_failed() and the Error_Handler() functions. When debugging the code it is observed that assert_failed() triggers when SystemClock_config() is called / executes. It looks like the HAL library got updated to use the variable 'uwTickPrio' in the function HAL_RCC_ClockConfig, instead of what was used in the older library, TICK_INT_PRIORITY. May ST please help me understand the reason why, 'uwTickPrio' is intentionally initialized to an invalid value. In order to fix the (assert_failed() function called) issue I have added uwTickPrio = TICK_INT_PRIORITY; inside function main() body, just before the comment: /* USER CODE END Init */s The code now works fine. Please help me with your inputs. Thanks, Rajeev

Key comments:
Hi @rxa1031, Thank you for this report. We tried to reproduce the issue you described, but we couldn't notice the problem. According to the following process of initializing the "uwTickPrio" variable to an invalid value, an update of the time base management is proposed to take into account low frequency systems where, at low frequency, a 1 ms systick interrupt does not allow to do anything else than a treated interrupt. uint32_t uwTickPrio = (1UL << __NVIC_PRIO_BITS); /* Invalid PRIO */ In HAL_InitTick() function, when checking the tick priority, it is better to relay on __NVIC_PRIO_BITS to check the tick priority limit of ticks instead of the initialized number (3 for M0, 15 for M4/M7). Thank you again for your contribution. Hi @RKOUSTM , I believe the reason for not observing the issue is that, either the FULL ASSERT related macro was not enabled or the tester did not place a break point inside the assert_failed() function body (or both). Please confirm whether, the tester enable FULL ASSERT in your test code? stm32h7xx_hal_conf.h must include: #define USE_FULL_ASSERT 1U Did the tester place a break point or a debug output message inside assert_failed() functi

HAL UART Init function already called) The words **"Peripheral not initialized"** present with explanation of bit b5 = 1 are confusing. I assume the UART RX related API is called only after the UART Driver is initialized, along with enabling required interrupts. Also, based on above information I expect value of HAL_UART_STATE_TIMEOUT should be 0x80U (i.e. bits [7:6] = 10) Without a clarity with bit b5 explanation I am not sure whether the HAL_UART_STATE_TIMEOUT should be 0xA0U. } if (HAL_UARTEx_SetRxFifoThreshold(&huart1, UART_RXFIFO_THRESHOLD_1_8) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } if (HAL_UARTEx_EnableFifoMode(&huart1) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } /* USER CODE BEGIN USART1_Init 2 */ if(IS_UART_RECEIVER_TIM EOUT_VALUE(2)) // earlier value dUSART1ReceiveTimeoutInBitsCount)) { HAL_UART_ReceiverTimeout_Config(&huart1, 2);// #DRA: modified for testing dUSART1ReceiveTimeoutInBitsCount); HAL_UART_EnableReceiverTimeout(&huart1); __HAL_UART_CLEAR_IT(&huart1, UART_CLEAR_RTOF); SET_BIT(huart1.Instance->CR1, USART_CR1_RTOIE); } else { dLEDShowError(dUSART1RxTimeoutTooLarge); } /* USER CODE END USART1_Init 2 */ } Asynchronous USART Receive call: uint8_t ucTestKey[2] = " \0"; if(dRxComplete == bIsAsyncUSART1ReceiveComplete) { bIsAsyncUSART1ReceiveComplete = dRxInProgress; } else { dLEDShowError(dBadUSART1RxComStateBeforeRxInitiate); assert_failed((uint8_t *)__FILE__, __LINE__); } __schedule_barrier(); if(HAL_OK != HAL_UART_Receive_IT(&huart1, (uint8_t *)ucTestKey, 1)) { dLEDShowError(dUSART1RxInitiationFailed); assert_failed((uint8_t *)__FILE__, __LINE__); } __schedule_barrier(); // // Here I want to check for HAL_UART_STATE_TIMEOUT, but function never returns HAL_UART_STATE_TIMEOUT. // while (HAL_UART_STATE_READY != HAL_UART_GetState(&huart1)) { __NOP(); } __schedule_barrier(); while(dRxInProgress == bIsAsyncUSART1ReceiveComplete) { __NOP(); } Please suggest a fix or a method for enabling Asynchronous UART Receive (interrupt) timeout. Regards, Rajeev

Key comments:
Hi @rxa1031, Actually, the point you raised has already been raised in another issue #31. We have discussed this internally and we are working on the implementation of a service to enable Reception Timeout interrupt. A fix will be made available in the frame of a future release. Regarding the second point, indeed, an error has been introduced in the comment which should rather be : * b5 Peripheral initialization status * 0 : Reset (Peripheral not initialized) diff -* 1 : Init done (Peripheral not initialized. HAL UART Init function already called) +* 1 : Init done (Peripheral initialized. HAL UART Init function already called) The same correction should be applied in the description of **RxState** bitmap. issues.issue_title: Issue with chosen MAX value (i.e. 56) of configMAX_PRIORITIES
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Issue with chosen MAX value (i.e. 56) of configMAX_PRIORITIES
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H753BIT6, component=FREERTOS, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=59
Root cause: Hi @rxa1031, Thank you for this report.
Fix: Hello, I was reviewing the FreeRTOS code and the CMSIS_OS2.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H753BIT6, Middleware, FREERTOS, usage_question, high, question, mw, rtos, CMSIS_OS2, configMAX_PRIORITIES, CMSIS-

Technical details:
Hello, I was reviewing the FreeRTOS code and the CMSIS_OS2.C file and the macro configMAX_PRIORITIES I assume the below statement is incorrect and I have a reason for it: /* CMSIS-RTOSv2 defines 56 levels of priorities. To be able to use them * all and avoid application misbehavior, configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION * must be set to 0 and configMAX_PRIORITIES to 56 * */ Even the declarations like below are incorrect: #define configMAX_PRIORITIES ( 56 ) **Observation 1:** The FreeRTOS code version 10.3.1 (and maybe earlier) have a file named blocktim.c at location FreeRTOSv10.3.1\FreeRTOS\Demo\Common\Minimal\blocktim.c The file declares the macro: #ifndef bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY #define bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY ( configMAX_PRIORITIES - 4 ) #endif I am not sure whether STM32CubeMX is aware of the above file or whether it has a different file in which above macro is created. **Observation 2:** File CMSIS_OS2.C declares the enum named osPriority_t, with the last three enumerated values as: osPriorityISR = 56, ///< Reserved for ISR deferred thread. osPriorityError = -1, ///< System cannot determine priority or illegal priority. osPriorityReserved = 0x7FFFFFFF ///< Prevents enum down-size compiler optimization. **Conclusion:** In order to allow code being ported to other microcontrollers (maybe non ST Microcontrollers) or debugged using MSVC, changes must be made to code. From observation 1, I believe all user implementations should only be allowed to use MAXIMUM PRIORITY value which is one less than bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY i.e. configMAX_PRIORITIES - 5 From observation 2 and above conclusion, I believe the value assigned to configMAX_PRIORITIES should be osPriorityISR + 5 Please share your opinion. Regards, @rxa1031

Key comments:
Hi @rxa1031, Thank you for this report. Unfortunately, for first point, we don't treat aspect related to FreeRTOS in our GitHub repositories. As the blocktim.c file is out of the scope of STMicroelectronics what about reporting this point to the [FreeRTOS GitHub](https://github.com/freertos)? Concerning the second point, the configMAX_PRIORITIES is set to 56 to support the osPriority in CMSIS V2 (see [this](https://www.keil.com/pack/doc/CMSIS_Dev/RTOS2/html/group__CMSIS__RTOS__ThreadMgmt.html) link). Please allow me to close this issue now. Thank you for your contribution. @RKOUSTM Thanks for sharing the response. I understand the point that you shared. The reason I reported the blocktim.c concern here is because I use Simulator (FreeRTOS\Demo\WIN32-MSVC\Win32.SLN) (and Visual Studio 2019) to sometimes debug my (STM32H753BIT6) code. Also if one wants to port the STM32CubeMX / ST provided FreeRTOS code to any other microcontroller or simulator then there might become a concern, as the informed file may get used and the person porting the code will not be aware that configMAX_PRIORITIES will have to be updated. @rxa1031

Problem: HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig not setting the HRTIM1 clock source
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-144, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=46
Root cause: Hi @andigandi, Thank you for this detailed report.
Fix: STM32 Nucleo-144 for STM32H743 Cube IDE 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-144, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, spotted before customer, STM32, STM32H743, IDE, HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig, RCC_HRTIM1CLK_CPUCLK

Technical details:
STM32 Nucleo-144 for STM32H743 Cube IDE 1.3.0 with STM32CubeH7 1.7.0 Description: Using HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig with PeriphClkInitStruct.Hrtim1ClockSelection = RCC_HRTIM1CLK_CPUCLK; with the intent of setting the clock source for HRTIM1 peripheral to the CPU clock has no effect. The problem seems to originate in stm32h7xx_hal_rcc_ex.c in line 1474. The function tries to check if the HRTIM1 peripheral does exist but it uses the wrong non-existing define HRTIM for that purpose: #if defined(HRTIM) /*------------------------------ HRTIM1 clock Configuration ----------------*/ if(((PeriphClkInit->PeriphClockSelection) & RCC_PERIPHCLK_HRTIM1) == RCC_PERIPHCLK_HRTIM1) { /* Check the parameters */ assert_param(IS_RCC_HRTIM1CLKSOURCE(PeriphClkInit->Hrtim1ClockSelection)); /* Configure the HRTIM1 clock source */ __HAL_RCC_HRTIM1_CONFIG(PeriphClkInit->Hrtim1ClockSelection); } #endif /*HRTIM*/ The file stm32h743xx.h defines HRTIM1 in line 2393. Changing the above code to use this define instead fixes the problem. The right clock source gets applied by HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig. #if defined(HRTIM1) /*------------------------------ HRTIM1 clock Configuration ----------------*/ if(((PeriphClkInit->PeriphClockSelection) & RCC_PERIPHCLK_HRTIM1) == RCC_PERIPHCLK_HRTIM1) { /* Check the parameters */ assert_param(IS_RCC_HRTIM1CLKSOURCE(PeriphClkInit->Hrtim1ClockSelection)); /* Configure the HRTIM1 clock source */ __HAL_RCC_HRTIM1_CONFIG(PeriphClkInit->Hrtim1ClockSelection); } #endif /*HRTIM1*/

issues.issue_title: FreeRTOS-MPU fails to run if its privileged RAM is in a cacheable memory region
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: FreeRTOS-MPU fails to run if its privileged RAM is in a cacheable memory region
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H743ZI2, component=FREERTOS, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=39
Root cause: Heads-up: I'm still finding this problem.
Fix: ## The setup - Hardware: Nucleo-H743ZI2 - IDE: IAR for Arm v8.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H743ZI2, Middleware, FREERTOS, bug_report, low, bug, internal bug tracker, mw, rtos, IDE, IAR

Technical details:
## The setup - Hardware: Nucleo-H743ZI2 - IDE: IAR for Arm v8.32.1 ## The bug FreeRTOS-MPU faults during initialization because of a cache coherency issue with pxCurrentTCB; allocated in the Privileged RAM region. The SDK example only works because the Privileged RAM section is allocated in DTCM, a non-cacheable memory region. To solve it, that memory region should be set as non-cacheable in the MPU. That way it can be allocated in cacheable memory regions. In more technical detail: - FreeRTOS-MPU allocates pxCurrentTCB in the privileged RAM section. - During xPortStartScheduler, the privileged RAM section is allocated in the MPU as cacheable - As a result, if the DCache is enabled, pxCurrentTCB will be cached. - Cache coherency is lost during the initialization of the RTOS' scheduler, the assembly routine vPortRestoreContextOfFirstTask attempts to access a Reserved memory region, and results in a hard fault ## How To Reproduce 0. Grab the FreeRTOS-MPU sample application from the SDK 1. Fix the FreeRTOS-MPU bug described in issue #38 so the MPU is enabled 2. Update the linker script and main.c to allocate the Privileged Data section into AXI ram instead of DTCM 3. If you're using different hardware than me, make sure the DCache is enabled and has access to the AXI SRAM region you set up in the previous step 4. Try to run the application, and you should get a crash right away. Or perhaps some other serious misbehavior, depending on which incorrect values are loaded into your registers from vPortRestoreContextOfFirstTask ## Additional context For a minimum viable fix, a couple of things need to be updated in each FreeRTOS-MPU port affected by this bug: 1. portmacro.h needs to support "normal, shareable, non-cacheable" configurations of MPU->RASR registers. That's TEX=001 S=1 B=0 C=0 according to [the docs](https://developer.arm.com/docs/dui0646/a/cortex-m7-peripherals/optional-memory-protection-unit/mpu-access-permission-attributes#BIHHEDAE): #define portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ( 0x0cUL << 16UL ) 2. Privileged RAM needs to be configured using that portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE **instead of** portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE. - In prvSetupMPU: portMPU_REGION_ATTRIBUTE_REG = ( portMPU_REGION_PRIVILEGED_READ_WRITE ) | #if 0 /* Original code */ ( portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE ) | #else /* fix */ ( portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ) | #endif prvGetMPURegionSizeSetting( ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_end__ - ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_start__ ) | ( portMPU_REGION_ENABLE ); - In vPortStoreTaskMPUSettings: xMPUSettings->xRegion[ 1 ].ulRegionAttribute = ( portMPU_REGION_PRIVILEGED_READ_WRITE ) | #if 0 /* Original code */ ( portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE ) | #else /* fix */ ( portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ) | #endif prvGetMPURegionSizeSetting( ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_end__ - ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_start__ ) | ( portMPU_REGION_ENABLE ); Alternatively, memory barriers could be used to ensure the coherency of pxCurrentTCB, but I was not successful in my attempts, and I'm not sure if other FreeRTOS variables would still be affected in more insidious ways. ## More context The fix described earlier got me past this problem, but I'm still running into other crashes shortly after. These may or may not have related causes; I'm still investigating. If you uncover any other issues while fixing this one, a heads-up would be greatly appreciated. Thanks, JC
